stories.title: Early-season check-in on new Rockets Marcus Smart and Bogdan Bogdanovic
stories.summary: Did Rafael Stone get it right again?
stories.detailText: With the season being roughly one-tenth of the way through, I figured we could do a check-in on the two of the major offseason acquisitions, Bogdan Bogdanovic and Marcus Smart, who were signed to contracts paying them $3,524,115 and $6,064,00 this season, respectively. Marcus Smart brings a lot more to the table for the Rockets than what appears in the box score. His defensive abilities, constant energy, and ability to make opposing guards miserable earned him Defensive Player of the Year honors in 2022. He brings another veteran presence to a young Rockets locker room. He will not be expected to score each night, but his ball-handling, shot creation, and the ability to make timely shots will make him a key piece of the Rockets’ rotation. So far thi s season, Marcus is averaging 9.8 points, 2.5 assists, 2.8 rebounds, and 1.3 steals while shooting 38.7% from three and 44.2% from the field. The field goal percentage is trending higher than his career average, as it three-point shooting, which is incredibly encouraging. Smart also had a stellar game vs. the Thunder, where he scored 24 points and made 7 three-pointers. Bogdan Bogdanovic provides the Rockets with a specific set of skills Houston needs perimeter shooting, and the 38% three-point shooter for his entire NBA career provides that. Bogdanovic can also create off the dribble at the second level of the offense and make shots when the main offensive players are on the bench or under heavy defensive pressure. He can create off the dribble at the second level of the offense and can make shots when the main offensive players are on the bench or under heavy pressure from the defense. This season , Bogdanovic is averaging 5.6 points per game, which does not seem like a lot, but he is shooting a blistering 45.5% from three. Any team can use that. Bogdanovic is an excellent attacking addition to this year’s sqaud. He can shoot, create off the dribble and space the floor, so he meets many of the Rockets’ needs. However, his health and consistency will determine the effectiveness of this signing. What is interesting about both of these acquisitions is the varying amounts of impact that each can bring to a game. Smart is brought in for his defense, energy, and leadership. Bogdanovic brings shooting, creation on offense, and floor spacing. Both players bring experience to Houston’s young core and can help ease the transition of some of the young players into more rotation minutes as they continue to grow. They can be of use to players like Reed Sheppard by having veteran players on the team to help support the young players and to allow for more flexibility with lineups. Ultimately, the value of both of these players will be determined by how they perform in games of consequence. Houston is trying to build a team of players that can help get them past the first round in the postseason, not just a collection of veterans and youngsters. If I had to give a grade for the two signings so far, I would give the Bogdonovic signing an A, and the Marcus Smart signing an A- only because Smart has missed time with an injury already. Thats all for today! Make sure to let me know what you all think about the signings in the comments, and as always make sure to check back at The Dream Shake for all things Houston Rockets coverage.

stories.summary: After an injury delayed his season debut, Adou Thiero shined in his first game on Friday.
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES, CA - NOVEMBER 6: Adou Thiero #1 of the Los Angeles Lakers boxes out during the game against the Portland Trail Blazers during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on November 6, 2026 at Crypto.Com Arena in Los Angeles, California. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Adam Pantozzi/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images One of the standouts of the early stages of the preseason was Adou Thiero, who looked to have built on a strong Summer League and was ready to be part of the Lakers’ rotation . However, an ill-timed injury halted Thiero’s progress and kept him out of the opening weeks of the regular season. After some patience to allow swelling in his knee to go down, Thiero finally made his season debut in Friday’s win over the Blazers and looked like he hadn’t missed a beat from the preseason. In only six minutes, Thiero’s impact was felt as he tallied four points, four rebounds and two assists. After the game, head coach JJ Redick was asked about his performance and got rave reviews. “I thought his first two defensive possessions, he made mistakes and then after that he was awesome,” Redick said. “He literally did everything we asked him to do. He was great on the offensive glass. Even sometimes when we didn’t necessarily get the possession, he was tapping the ball and crashing. “I thought the read he made out of the short roll, I think they blitzed three times in the first half and two of those were against him. He makes the short roll and he gets the lob. I thought he played a great game and, defensively, he was really good in the second half.” Thiero came in late in the first quarter in the role previously held by Jarred Vanderbilt and immediately made an impact. Given his leaping ability, Thiero being the ball screener and roll man felt like an obvious fit. The Blazers immediately tested him as they blitzed Luka Dončić, forcing Thiero to not just be in the right spot in the short roll, but then make a decision. He nailed both aspects, setting up Ziaire Williams for a dunk. Adou Thiero roll draws two tags (Mamu and Ziaire's men). Thiero finds Ziaire for the lob. https://t.co/eAxPLWNKy7 pic.twitter.com/0FIBwwHwBV — Connor Moreno (@cmorenoNBA) November 7, 2026 Shortly after, the Blazers opted for a more traditional pick-and-roll coverage. This time, Thiero rolled hard to the rim and caught the lob for an athletic finish. LUKA TO ADOU pic.twitter.com/NuoLMrAlcN — Lakers Empire (@LakersEmpire) November 7, 2026 “He did great,” Walker Kessler said of Thiero. “Obviously, we value Adou a lot. He’s a very physical player. Really talented, athletic player. I mean, that lob he caught is very, very impressive. He had a really good debut for the season.” Thiero’s athleticism is unparalleled on the roster — and among the elites of the elite in the league as a whole — and offers the Lakers a different dynamic. Thiero as a screener and roller won’t always work as it did on Friday, but his athleticism and activity level will continue to jump off the screen. The Lakers’ hope now is that he can stay healthy and start to stack positive performances in the regular season. stories.title: Den Questions: Finding Identity In Turmoil
stories.summary: Ten games in the Wolves have burned bright, weathered losses, and still have questions to answer.
stories.detailText: Welcome back to the Den. The Wolves are ten games in and their record stands at 7-3. Over that time the Wolves sprinted out of the gates, lost Anthony Edwards to dirty knees in need of a cleaning, and have mostly righted the ship. Their losses are on travel back-to-backs and their first game without Edwards where they didn’t even have a chance to practice before tip-off. This team found something special in their first four games and then had their literal knees cut from them. Through the mire of the early season, as the rest of the league reels from their own injuries, the Wolves are looking for another new identity. An identity that does not include Edwards but prepares for his return. As you can imagine, there are a lot of questions for this team to answer. Here are some of them. Note: So much of this is small sample size theater. 1. Can Jonathan Kuminga keep this up? It’s just flashes. He had similar highs in Golden State before cooling down. There’s no way he can keep this up. Here he goes again driving into traffic to get blocked… huh, nice pass. No no no, don’t shoot tha…SPLASH! Oh my gawd, he got up so high for that rebound. This short-staged drama has occurred inside my head in nearly every game this year. In good games and bad, Jonathan Kuminga has shown up to do whatever is asked of him. In every counting stat except points per game, Kuminga is averaging career bests; rebounds (5.7), assists (2.9), steals (1.2) and blocks (1.0). His highest BPM through his first five seasons was 0.1. This season he is at 2.9 and has his career first positive for Offensive Box Plus Minus (0.6). Head Coach Chris Finch has heaped praise on JK. In Minnesota’s more read and react, flow, style, the Wolves starting power forward is emboldened to make a play when the ball finds him. His cuts aren’t always rewarded but it sends the defense into a panic and opens things up for his teammates. It also puts him in the middle of the floor to grab or poke out offensive rebounds. I am running out of excuses for why it won’t last. After the first few games, I thought his play would disappear once the initial novelty of the season’s start wore off. It didn’t. I thought he’d become more shot hungry and ball dominant when Ant went down. He hasn’t. I thought he’d get worn down having to guard some of the best players in the league night after night. This might happen as the overlong season grinds on, but so far Kuminga seems to get up for the battle. The hardest question might be coming, “Can the Wolves afford to keep Kuminga?“ 2. What is Rudy’s purpose on offense? The start of the season has seen a dramatic drop in Rudy Gobert’s points per game and his near league-best shooting efficiency. Gobert is averaging his fourth fewest shot attempts, second least points per game, the worst shooting percentage, and worst free throw percentage of his career. It took one of the smartest basketball minds in Mike Conley over a year to learn how to play with Rudy. LaMelo Ball has had a scant few weeks to build chemistry. Combine that with the geometry of the floor and the defensive attention he is getting due to the sidelined Edwards, and it’s no surprise the lack of consistency. The Wolves need Rudy to be effective on offense. The book is out on the big man. Good defenses know how to bait Minnesota into thinking Rudy is open and recover quick enough to force a turnover or an errant shot. Which brings us to the question of how to effectively use Gobert on offense. There is space to use him in the pick n’ roll, but that has rarely been Finch’s play style of choice. He is averaging a career high in offensive rebounds and this is primarily where I want him to find his points. Finishing those misses just as they bounce off or tipping them out to teammates to try again when defenders are too close to him. Don’t give them a chance to send him to the line. He is very good at screening his teammates open and should continue to be used as the effective body in the way. This opens up Ball, Ayo Dosunmu, and Bones Hyland to get a screen assist into open triples. But this also pulls Rudy away from the hoop and the offensive boards that are his best offense. Simple as it sounds his threat to roll is only as effective as his chemistry with his point guard. Until that firms up, he’s on cleanup duty. 3. What is a Ghost Screen? The Wolves are getting spooky with a lot more ghost screens this season. This gambit, that asks a shooting threat to feint a screen before sprinting to the other side of the point-of-attack (POA) defender, is meant to short circuit a defense. In a fraction of a second, the ghost screener’s defender has to determine if they need to call for a switch if the screen gets set, or to chase after the shooter who has suddenly burst to a preferred place to spot up. The Wolves are loaded with players who can quickly turn on the jets (I can’t recommend Ayo Dosumnu’s Player’s Tribune piece enough) and make this decision that much harder. Screens are overcome best when a defense is communicating. The threat of a ghost screen shortens that window for effective communication. If the POA defender thinks a screen is about to be set, they might get ready to hedge for the incoming contact giving the ball handler enough wiggle room to drive. If the chase defender thinks a screen is being set, they might slow up enough to give the ghost screener a chance to find an open look. If a screen is set, the game flows into common pick n’ roll, one of the most tried and true means of creating advantages. In the clip below, the Wolves use a combination of screens to break Orlando’s zone, a past bugaboo for Minnesota. Armed with better outside shooting than the past two years, look for the Wolves to continue to haunt perimeter defenders with these scary non-screens. 4. Who else has come back from dirty knees? Note: Every injury to a player is unique. No timeline to return or level of ability when returning is the same. An Achilles tear for Donte DiVincenzo and his play style is a completely different injury that an Achilles tear for Ariel Hukporti and how he approaches the game, despite hurting the same tendon. The day after it was announced that Ant would get arthroscopic knee surgery, a friend of mine sent me a grim text. All he could think of was Grant Hill, Brandon Roy, and Penny Hardaway and the possibility that Ant’s career would be sapped from him like it had from those elite athletes. I immediately texted back “What about DWade, Kobe, CP3?” After a brief internet search here are several NBA players who have undergone arthroscopic knee surgery who had some of their best years after the fact. Kobe Bryant – Kobe had his first knee surgery in 2003, another in 2006, and another in 2010. In the midst of this string of surgeries he was an All-Star every year (despite the Laker bump, these were earned), won an MVP and was top five in MVP voting in all but one year, and made All-Defensive Teams in every year but one. Dwyane Wade – DWade (a frequent Ant comp) had his entire left meniscus removed in 2002 while in college and went on to have a Hall of Fame career where he was unwillingly nicknamed Flash for how quick he was despite playing sans knee cartilage. Chris Paul – Snitch Paul had arthroscopic knee surgery to repair a meniscus tear in 2010 while still with the New Orleans Hornets. As fun as he was on those Hornets teams, the Point God emerged into a force in the years after with the Lob City Clippers, Hardenball Rockets, and even made his first Finals with the Phoenix Suns, 11 years after the surgery. Jimmy Butler – General Soreness had surgery on his right knee in 2018 while the Wolves were third in the Western Conference. He returned to help break the 14 year playoff drought. Jimmy has since been the driving force to two NBA finalist teams, never winning one. He adds multiple All-Star selection, an All-NBA selection, and an All-Defensive Team honor to his otherwise championship barren trophy case. I’m not bitter. Jaylen Brown – Mr. Lamb Chops and Gravy had a knee procedure in the summer of 2025 and was back by training camp en route to being an All-Star, All-NBA 2nd Team, and sixth in MVP voting. This surgery to clean up Ant’s knee will likely diminish Ant’s burst athleticism. He has moved his game to more outside shooting while maintaining a rim presence. If his downhill game is not as quick, it will hurt, but he’s also added a midrange for if the defender goes too far under that leaves him a three level problem for any defense. Plenty of NBA greats have bounced back, here’s hoping Ant joins this laudable list. 5. What does this rotation look like fully healthy? Ant is out for roughly two months. Terrance Shannon Jr. has missed two games with a hip contusion. Donte DiVincenzo is recovering from an Achilles tear with every intention of coming back this season. In their absence the Wolves have slotted Ayo Dosunmu into the starting lineup. Bones Hyland is scoring the ball well. Jaylen Clark is getting into guys jerseys and hitting 41.2% of his threes on 2.1 attempts a game. All of these players are competing with each other for minutes. While the deeper bench has done yeomen’s work to keep the Wolves head above water, they are not as good as the players whose minutes they are sopping up. Finch is strict in his rotations. In the last three years, his starting lineups are in the top five for most used lineups in the NBA. If he gets a fully healthy team, Bones and Clark’s minutes will likely disappear all together. Ayo will move back into his sixth man role ready to be whatever his team needs of him. Donte is the biggest question mark. He started all 82 games last season, but there is not a spot for him in this starting lineup. We also don’t know what he will look like coming back from such a devastating injury. Sans LaMelo foul trouble giving Bones more minutes in the Raptors game, Finch has only given double digit minutes out to nine players before the injuries started. Joan Beringer’s minutes aren’t going anywhere. Trey Lyles has size, outside shooting, and has shown a predilection for being in the right place at the right time. Unless countering a specific lineup, his minutes stay the same. Shannon figures to be the first cut in playtime with the Big Ragu’s return unless Finch expands his bench to ten. And yet, there are few players who could elevate TJ’s game better than Donte. An attacking TJ off a Beringer screen with Donte, Ayo, and Trey spreading the floor is tailormade to confound defenses. On those nights where the injury report is blank, I hope Finch keeps the pedal to the metal with frequent rotations in the vein of Memphis Grizzlies coach Tuomas Iisalo. The Grizz have 13 players averaging double digit minutes and only two players over 30 minutes a game, Cameron Boozer (32.3) and Ty Jerome (30.7). The NBA season is grueling. We have seen year after year the Wolves struggle as the playoffs wear on. TJ, Bones, and Clark are good players, deserving of minutes that will keep the starters fresh for when they are needed most. 6. How do the Wolves compare to the rest of the league (through 10)? Look here for the inarguable answers through the first ten games. The Wolves are presently top five in the league in the following team categories: Points per Game (5th) Rebounds Per Game (1st) Three Pointers Made (2nd) Net Rating (1st) Defensive Rating (3rd) 2nd Chance Points (5th) Pull Up Shooting (5th) Loose Balls Recovered (2nd) The Net Rating stat is leaning heavily on Minnesota’s first three blow out wins. That said, they have only lost their games by a combined 17 points thus far. They are hitting plenty of threes. They are defending with energy and diving for loose balls. They don’t treat the game as something that should be handed to them like some legacy Ivy Leaguer applying at his dad’s company. They are battling for the ball and snatching it from less hungry competition. 7. What is the ranking of the Wolves’ ticket package/giveaways this season? Gone are the days of XL T-Shirts and Howl Towels. The Wolves have overloaded this season with all manner of tchotchke, curio and baseball jersey to lure fans and collectors alike to home games. Most of these do not have an image released but give you just enough information to send your imagination whirring. There is an entire series of baseball hats with design help from former Wolves vets. For Kevin Garnett’s jersey retirement, Minnesota has five unique pieces of career spanning collectible celebrating the Big Ticket’s accomplishments wearing 21. There are bobbleheads, blankets, and backpacks and way way way too many baseball jerseys. And here they all are , definitively ranked. 8. Why are there so many baseball jersey giveaway nights? To begin, I know: There are seven ticket package giveaways featuring a baseball jersey this season. In collaboration with local artists, this is what the Wolves are doing for their Artist’s Series this year. Each jersey, for a sport different than the one it is honoring, celebrates a societal cross-section; Latino Noche, Military Appreciation, Native American Heritage, Pride Night, Asian American and Pacific Islander Night, Black Excellence, and Inspiring Women. I think the designs are fun. Each one is a variation with pin stripes in a variety of colors. Some of them have designs on the sleeve nodding to the theme of the night. All of them have “Wolves Basketball” on the back. And all of them are baseball jerseys. I love the Artist’s series. I have purchased at least one shirt each of the last two seasons. I love that a local artist gets to put their stamp on the Wolves design. I love that several of the local artists are BIPOC and women creators. I love that they came in a variety of T-shirts, sweatshirts, and hats. I just don’t understand the thought process in making seven different baseball jerseys. I don’t know enough about production costs, or textiles, so forgive my potentially ignorant question, but, wouldn’t a jersey with two less sleeves of material be cheaper while closer to the topic at hand? Can they not do basketball jerseys because of some contractual stuff with Nike? WHY!? All that said, I think the Native American design is my favorite and I might need to get one. 9. Where are we at in the marathon? MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA – NOVEMBER 02: LaMelo Ball #1 of the Minnesota Timberwolves celebrates his three-point basket against the Milwaukee Bucks in the first quarter at Target Center on November 02, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Wolves have played ten games in 17 days. If losing Ant and TJ wasn’t enough, they have not had more than a day between games and twice have played in travel back-to-backs. All marathons are tough. Some like to remind you of that fact in the first few miles. The giddy win streak to start the season, like those first marathon steps past gathered supporters, can make you feel invincible. Before you know it, you’re running faster than you can sustain and its only mile two. This is not to say that what we saw in the first three games is unsustainable, but with Ant out, the team is grasping for an identity while still playing fast and loose. LaMelo is trying to play aggressive defense and fouling like crazy. The race is still young though. The stored ATP that let the Wolves sprint out of the gate may be spent, but they have years of experience and the benefits of youth. In the first full month of the season, they are searching for a pace they can maintain. The challenge of racing a marathon is knowing the line between speed and overheating. The Wolves need to keep chasing after rebounds and through screens without losing anyone else to injury. If the news of Donte’s return holds true, and Ant and TJ bounce back, they’ll get an injection of energy better than any banana or unsavory gel packet found along the march. 10. Where will the Wolves be at Game 21? HOUSTON, TEXAS – NOVEMBER 04: LaMelo Ball #1 of the Minnesota Timberwolves shoots the ball against the Houston Rockets during the second half at Toyota Center on November 04, 2026 in Houston, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) | Getty Images From now until the day after Thanksgiving (no it is not a holiday and you can’t make me recognize it as one) the Wolves take on a mix of the top and bottom of both conferences. They play nine of them at home. Here’s a snap shot of who they got. The promise that the Utah Jazz were going to try this year has landed on its face due to injury and their inability to defend the point of attack. The Bulls are finally rebuilding. The Nets have five players in their sophomore season and only two of them get playing time despite their abysmal record. On the challenging side of the opposition, Cooper Flagg looks incredible alongside the returned Kyrie Irving. The Mavericks are a deep squad and can hang around in any game. The Memphis Grizzlies, on the back of Ty Jerome’s electric start and the connective play of rookie Cam Boozer are near the top of the conference. Portland Trail Blazer’s head coach Micah Nori returns to Minnesota for a home back-to-back. Nori has his team cooking, bolstered by Blazer legend, the renewed Damian Lillard. The Knicks have started off shaky but can find their championship form on any given night. Finally, the Thunder are a battered and broken team that still boasts seven players that could earn starter’s minutes on most teams in the league. With the Wolves only having one back to back in this stretch, and three days of rest between game 11 and 12 to rest and practice, I see the Wolves going into the month of December playing at the same pace, 14-6. So Canis, what questions do you have?

stories.title: Wizards' Trae Young calls Atlanta return a 'cool' experience despite loss
stories.summary: Trae Young faced his former team, the Hawks, on the court in Atlanta for the first time since joining the Wizards.
stories.detailText: ATLANTA -- After Trae Young was introduced last for the Washington Wizards on Friday night, he took the court before tipoff, went to the corner of the floor and settled himself. Then he jogged over to Atlanta Hawks coach Quin Snyder for a pregame embrace before taking on his former team. "I don't even know how to describe the feeling," Young said after the Hawks topped the Wizards 139-132 . "I mean, it was different. It was cool for me." Young had 23 points and 10 assists but also a season-high nine turnovers against the Hawks, who beat the Wizards in both games of a home-and-home series this week. Young said he didn't get a chance to chat with Snyder in Washington, so he wanted to make sure he said hello Friday because he has a special relationship with his former coach. Young was a four-time All-Star with the Hawks in seven-plus seasons before being traded to the Wizards for Corey Kispert and CJ McCollum in January. He is the franchise's all-time leader in assists and 3-pointers. He returned to Atlanta last year after he was traded but was unable to play because of an injured knee. He was on the bench when the Hawks ran a tribute video during a second-quarter timeout highlighting his time in Atlanta and showed appreciation for the cheering fans by making a heart with his hands. On Friday night, Young was healthy and ready to play. There were a few cheers when he was introduced, but it was mostly a muted response. Young said he will remember his first night in an opposing jersey. "I don't think it'll feel like this every time, but definitely tonight," Young said. "Just even, even the day we played them [Wednesday], I knew today was coming next. I'm not gonna get a first all the time. You know what I'm saying?" Young entered Friday leading the NBA in assists with 9.3 per game. Wizards coach Brian Keefe praised Young's unselfishness before the game. "He's fully embraced the group, and he's trying to make each one of these guys better and put us in good positions," Keefe said. "He's done a really good job of that."

stories.title: Luka Doncic is soaring, Lakers are No. 1 in West. His brilliance is leaving mark

stories.detailText: Lakers coach JJ Redick was stumped. He had recently likened Luka Dončić to a supernova. He said you have to pick your poison against him. So, when asked if he had any superlatives to offer following Dončić’s 53-point, five-rebound, five-assist performance in the Lakers’ 124-118 win over the Trail Blazers on Friday, Redick stumbled. “Sure,” Redick said. “Sure.” When a reporter started asking another question, he interjected. “I’m going to just sit around, we’ll gather one day and come up with more superlatives,” Redick added. “So I’ll have more words ready. But for now, I don’t have any words.” The hyper-prepared Lakers coach was finally ill-prepared for an assignment. Redick isn’t the only person who has been left dumbfounded following Dončić’s blazing start to the season in which he’s averaging a league-leading 40.1 points, 7.7 rebounds and 7.6 assists . In Friday’s game, Dončić passed Michael Jordan (347) for the most points scored in the firstnine games of a season since the NBA-ABA merger with 361 points. Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic shoots a free throw during an NBA basketball game against the Portland Trail Blazers in Los Angeles, Friday, Nov. 6, 2026. AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill It’s the most points anyone has scored in the modern NBA since Wilt Chamberlain in 1962-63. “I’m having a lot of fun,” Dončić said. “Obviously playing basketball, it’s a lot of fun for me. It’s more [fun] when you play like this and when you win games. So, it’s been like this my whole life. Basketball was my dream. Playing in the NBA was my dream. Just living my dream.” The Lakers are living theirs, too. The 27-year-old face of their franchise is having an MVP-caliber campaign while leading the Lakers to the No. 1 seed in the Western Conference with an 8-2 record. No one expected the Lakers to be this good. And no one expected Dončić to soar to the top of the MVP conversation after he hadn’t finished in the top two in voting ever in his career. Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic, left, drives to the basket against Portland Trail Blazers center Robert Williams III on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026, in Los Angeles. AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill But if the first few weeks of the season have made anything clear, it’s that Redick needs to beef up his vocabulary. He needs to get a thesaurus. Dončić is skyrocketing, and he’s carrying the Lakers with him. There were many incredible moments in the Lakers’ 16-point come-from-behind win over the Trail Blazers in which they stormed back after shooting 4-for-23 from beyond the arc in the first half, including missing all 15 of their initial attempts from that distance. There was the buzzer-beating 62-foot shot that Dončić made at the end of the second quarter, a shot he literally banked in from three-quarters of the court. “Luka can do some things that maybe a handful, if not no one, can do in basketball,” Redick said. Things only got more fun from there. Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic, left, shoots over Portland Trail Blazers center Robert Williams III on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026, in Los Angeles. AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill There was a little mixup after Dončić notched his 11th 50-point performance in his career, surpassing Kareem Abdul-Jabbar for 10th-most such games in NBA history. It all started because Ziaire Williams couldn’t wait to congratulate Dončić. So much so that Williams decided to interrupt what he thought was Dončić’s walk-off television interview with “NBA on Prime” by approaching him from behind, putting his hands on his shoulders and yelling, “Fifty ball.” Only, there was a problem. Austin Reaves was doing the interview. Not Dončić. “ I’m the wrong white person ,” said Reaves, who had 25 points. Did Williams seriously confuse his two teammates? “Deadass,” he said, flashing a smile in the Lakers’ locker room. Dončić got in on the fun, too. “That was very disrespectful to me,” Dončić said jokingly of being confused with Reaves, with whom he shares a brotherly bond . It has been a wild stretch for Dončić, who’s shattering records nightly. He’s leaving his coach at a loss for words. He’s making shots from outer space. And he’s leaving his teammates seeing his face in everyone. So, only one question remains. Can Dončić keep this up? “I feel like that,” he said. “But as long as we win, I’m good.”

Emirates Cup action raised the intensity and the Mavs stepped up to the tune of a 112-100 win Friday night . 63-45: Rebound disparity in favor of Dallas For what felt like the first time in a long time, the Mavs dominated on the boards to the tune of +18 for the night. Dallas knew this was something they needed to work on and they answered the call Friday night. The cherry on top was that rookie Morez Johnson, Jr. led all players 17 boards! 20-5: Mavs’ second chance points advantage All of those rebounds led to plenty of points for Dallas. They made the most of ending Utah possessions and extending their own possessions, outscoring the Jazz by 15 in second chance points. 31-14: Free throw disparity in favor of Dallas The Mavericks got themselves to the line early and often, allowing them to keep the game tight in the first half. Utah was more efficient from the line, missing only a single attempt, but Dallas’ 80.6% (25-of-31) was more than enough of an edge, giving the Mavs a +12 advantage from the charity stripe. 9: Number of traveling calls The game had an inordinate number of traveling calls; nine to be exact. In the flow of the game, it was quite noticeable and somewhat bizarre. The travel-happy referees were equal opportunity penalizers, handing Utah five of the infractions, and Dallas four of their own. 28-6: Mavericks scoring run Dallas opened up a tight game in the third quarter and early part of the fourth. Reeling off a 28-6 scoring run, Dallas extended a one possession game to a 20-point lead. Utah responded with a couple of three-point makes and a smaller run of their own, but that 28-6 run proved to be the deciding factor in a Mavericks’ win. The Mavs needed a win to wash away a bit of the stink from the prior two games and they did all the little things to make it happen against the Jazz. Dallas was locked in on the boards, got to the line, and put together a nice run to build a cushion that proved insurmountable for the Jazz. stories.title: Oso Ighodaro is starting; is that a good thing?
stories.summary: The Suns need Oso's versatility today while giving Maluach the time and experience necessary to grow into his potential.
stories.detailText: PHOENIX, AZ - NOVEMBER 5: Oso Ighodaro #11 of the Phoenix Suns grabs the rebound during the game against the Orlando Magic on November 5, 2026 at Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix, Arizona. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Kate Frese/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The Phoenix Suns moved Oso Ighodaro into the starting lineup for Thursday’s win against the Orlando Magic. Many called for a change to the lineup (or multiple changes , which is another article for another day). He is a somewhat polarizing player, with staunch fans and outspoken skeptics. I’ll make a case for this being absolutely the right move for this team, right now. Khaman Maluach is learning game by game. Working on his body (and hopefully hands) to get stronger. He has an awesome frame and, at 20 years old, is just beginning to learn the nuances of NBA success. He has a mostly high effort level and wants to be good. However, the NBA is littered with players thrust into action before developing properly – and then losing confidence, picking up bad habits. Time on the court in meaningful minutes is needed to progress toward the objective of becoming a solid NBA starting center. The current situation with Mark Williams out well into 2027 allows for consistent 15-20 minute nights. Handing the “starter” keys could put him on a path more closely aligned to former Suns top-10 pick Josh Jackson (sorry to those with draft PTSD here). Back to Oso. The Phoenix starting lineup needs more connectivity and flow on offense? Check. Struggling horrifically on defense? Check. Per HoopsJunkie.io , Ighodaro’s on/off defensive rating of -17.2 points per 100 possessions ranks EIGHTH in the NBA! This is in spite of being a below-average defensive rebounder (141st in the NBA in DREB%). Keep in mind, he suffered a right oblique strain in the opener and is likely just rounding back into form now. I’ve referenced DARKO several times as a great tool to project overall player value at a moment in time. Through last season, his projected value was steadily growing. Once fully healthy, it is reasonable to expect that progression to continue. He looks bigger and stronger. His turnovers are down. While the results are not there yet at the free-throw line, he looks smoother (and commentators have noticed the same). With a DARKO of 1.0, compared to a -1.6 for Maluach, the model predicts more positive impact on winning in the present. Oso and Ryan Dunn, to an even greater extent early this season, are developing players. They show what development can look like for players drafted 40th and 28th, respectively. With his raw talents (drafted 10th) and willingness to work, Maluach’s ultimate success depends on development done the right way. This franchise needs Man Man to get there for the long run – and needs Oso right now to stabilize a starting lineup that was in disarray.

stories.title: Luka Doncic's historic run jump-starts early MVP conversation
stories.summary: Lakers guard Luka Doncic's teammates and opposing coaches are in awe of his blistering scoring so far this season, fueling early support for MVP honors.
stories.detailText: Lakers guard Luka Doncic makes a behind-the-back pass in front of three Portland Trail Blazers at Crypto.com Arena on Friday. (Gina Ferazzi / Los Angeles Times) Ten games is too early for most valuable player conversation. Just don’t tell fans at Crypto.com Arena. “M-V-P! M-V-P!” the Lakers faithful chant at Luka Doncic every time the Lakers guard toes the free-throw line. After dropping a season-high 53 points during the Lakers’ 124-118 win over the Portland Trail Blazers on Friday, Doncic is averaging 40.1 points, 7.8 rebounds and 7.7 assists in a scoring binge for the ages. He’s the fourth Laker to have four consecutive games of 40 or more points. He’s the third to have seven games of 35 or more points. And he’s doing it efficiently: Doncic’s sky-high shooting percentage dipped to 49.8% after an unusually cold 5-for-15 shooting night from three-point range Friday. He was still 12 for 18 from two-point range. Here are three takeaways from Friday’s win: Too early to tell? Lakers guard Luka Doncic shouts after sinking a three-pointer that gave the Lakers a five-point lead over Portland in the third quarter Friday at Crypto.com Arena. (Gina Ferazzi / Los Angeles Times) Walker Kessler just shook his head as he grasped for the right words. There might not be many more left to describe what Doncic is doing. “He’s my MVP,” the Lakers center said eventually. Being in the most valuable player conversation isn’t new for Doncic. The two-time scoring champion finished third in MVP voting in 2024 with Dallas. He averaged 33.9 points, 9.2 rebounds and 9.8 assists during the regular season, then led the Mavericks to the NBA Finals. Each season the do-it-all guard is among the favorites to win the award. But Doncic’s early-season campaign feels different. Not only is Doncic in great shape, Portland coach Micah Nori said before Friday’s game, but Doncic also has the right pieces around him after the Lakers remade their roster to complement the star with floor-spacing shooters, strong perimeter defenders and a rolling center. “It’s a perfect offensive storm,” Nori said. “He’s the MVP right now. Hands down.” LUKA JUST SANK IT FROM 3/4 COURT 🤯 Bruce Springsteen can’t believe what he just witnessed! pic.twitter.com/D0a9aSnwuX — NBA (@NBA) November 7, 2026 Lakers coach JJ Redick does not engage in MVP discussion until 50 games in, he said. When told Doncic topped NBA.com’s first MVP ladder Friday , the Lakers coach brushed aside any chance to make a grand proclamation. In the premature MVP rankings, Doncic was ahead of San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama . The 22-year-old is averaging 29.1 points, 12.6 rebounds, three assists and 4.2 blocks per game. Doncic’s 53-point outburst eclipsed Wembanyama’s 52 points the star center scored Wednesday for the highest single-game scoring performance this season. But Wembanyama also grabbed 24 rebounds with eight blocks in a historic statline matched only by Wilt Chamberlain. The French superstar finished second in MVP voting last year and was the first unanimous defensive player of the year in league history. His outsized defensive impact was a significant part of why he entered the season as the betting favorite to win his first MVP. Read more: Swanson: Luka Doncic can lead Lakers to a title, but only if his teammates pull their weight Doncic, who didn’t get any votes from NBA general managers when asked in a preseason survey who they thought would win the MVP, said he’s determined to step up on defense for his team. He is averaging 1.7 steals per game, which ranks second among Lakers players. His four drawn charges is tied for most in the league. “He has a pride and he has a hunger,” Lakers forward Sandro Mamukelashvili said of Doncic’s defense. “He has a will to not be labeled as that guy who you can just attack.” Doncic is challenging Chamberlain’s stats on the offensive end. His 361 points through his first nine games are the most for a player since Chamberlain’s 472 points in 1962-63. No one has averaged 40 points over a season since the legendary center in 1963. The possibility has barely crossed Doncic’s mind. “As long as we win, I’m good,” Doncic said. The Lakers are 8-2 with the best record in the Western Conference. They have not started 8-2 since their last championship season. Welcome back Lakers forward Adou Thiero drives to the basket between Portland's Scoot Henderson (00) and Jrue Holiday (5) at Crypto.com Arena on Friday. (Gina Ferazzi / Los Angeles Times) Adou Thiero had a loud four points, four rebounds and two assists in his long-awaited season debut Friday. The energetic forward missed the first nine games of the season because of swelling in his left knee. He didn’t waste any time reintroducing himself to the team, keeping a loose ball alive on his first offensive possession that led to an offensive rebound and a put-back from Mamukelashvili. “He literally did everything we asked him to do,” Redick said. The second-year forward has been hampered by his balky left knee since college, when he missed the end of his junior season after surgery. The procedure delayed the beginning of his rookie season and when he returned, a sprained MCL in his right knee knocked him out for six more weeks. The injuries prevented Thiero from gaining any traction. This summer, when he had the longest stretch of sustained health during his short professional career, he could finally show teammates and coaches what he could do. Thiero jumped out of the gym during practices. He smothered teammates while guarding the ball. He brought the same energy to the court Friday when it counted. “We value Adou a lot,” Kessler said. “He’s a very physical player, really talented, athletic player.” Defensive backup plan Lakers forwards Ziaire Williams, left, and Sandro Mamukelashvili double team Portland guard Sidy Cissoko as he attempts a layup at Crypto.com Arena on Friday. (Gina Ferazzi / Los Angeles Times) The Lakers missed their first 15 three-point shots. It felt like a minor miracle they trailed by only seven at halftime. The most dynamic offense in the league had to rely on its defense. The Lakers forced 24 turnovers and held the Trail Blazers (6-2) to 15 points in the third quarter. “It’s nice to know when you’re not making shots that you can also rely on your defense to help keep you in the game,” said forward Jake LaRavia , who had seven points, eight rebounds and one steal. The Lakers rank 21st in defensive rating, giving up 113.6 points per 100 possessions. They are one of the worst rebounding teams in the league, ranking 29th despite outrebounding the Trail Blazers by three. Their defense instead relies on blocks and steals. The Lakers are tied for third in the NBA with 10.7 steals per game. Matisse Thybulle leads the team with 1.8 steals per game. Austin Reaves had a team-high four steals Friday. Sign up for our weekly newsletter on all things Lakers. This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

stories.title: In Cleveland return, LeBron James struggles to find 'good rhythm' in 76ers' loss
stories.summary: Returning to Cleveland as the opposition for the third time in a different NBA uniform, LeBron James struggled against the Cavaliers, finishing with eight points on 3-for-12 shooting with six turnovers in Philadelphia's 119-96 NBA Cup loss.
stories.detailText: CLEVELAND -- The atmosphere in Rocket Arena on Friday night wasn't the "depths of hell," as LeBron James said he experienced when he first returned to this venue wearing a Miami Heat jersey 16 years ago, but James' play was something out of a hellish nightmare. James had one of the worst games of his career in Friday night's 119-95 NBA Cup loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers , finishing with eight points on 3-for-12 shooting and six turnovers. The porous night ended James' 396-game streak of scoring at least 10 points in Cleveland; the last time he scored fewer than 10 points in Cleveland was Dec. 29, 2004, a day before his 20th birthday. It was James' first time back in Cleveland since the Cavaliers' failed offseason pursuit of the 41-year-old this summer, when he chose to join the Sixers over the Cavaliers, Heat, Golden State Warriors and Minnesota Timberwolves in free agency. "That first day or two, you're just like, you're depressed, quite honestly," Cavaliers coach Kenny Atkinson said last month about losing out on James. James received a warm welcome, as most fans in the arena stood to cheer, giving him louder roars than all of the Cavaliers starters. And yet, James seemed indifferent to the welcoming response. After all, he had returned to Cleveland with two other teams -- the Heat and Los Angeles Lakers -- but that feeling ultimately comes from a fraught night James can never forget. "At the end of the day, nothing can get worse than Dec. 2, 2010, from a reception standpoint," James said. "So I've seen the depths of hell when it comes to reception here, all the way to the heavens above. So anything in between is easy money." James returned to Cleveland in December 2010 after he joined the Heat in free agency. James, who was 25 at the time, was mercilessly booed by the fans, and on that night, it seemed as though they would never reconcile with the superstar who broke their hearts when he made his decision to leave his hometown team during the national television special.​ To add to their heartbreak, James took the taunts and ridicule in stride, scoring 38 points and leading the Heat to a 118-90 rout over his former team. Sixteen years later, James, now with gray hairs in his beard, gave a performance the crowd in 2010 would have feasted on. He struggled to blow by Cavaliers defenders, his shots were off target, and he turned the ball over six times. For the first time, he looked like he was playing in his 24th NBA season. "I know I damn sure wasn't good at all," James said. James wasn't the only Sixer who struggled Friday night. The other former MVP on the team, Joel Embiid , also had one of the worst games of his career, finishing 0-for-9 from the field with six points. It was the second-worst shooting performance of his career; he went 0-of-11 from the field against the Toronto Raptors seven years ago. James and Embiid became the third former MVP duo in NBA history to each score in single digits and shoot 25% or worse from the field in the same game. "I definitely did not feel in a good rhythm offensively," James said. "We didn't look like much offensively. ... Too many turnovers on my behalf, and I didn't feel in a rhythm." The Sixers (8-2) will play the Bulls in Chicago on Sunday. "Tonight was not our shot, not our greatest of shots," James said. "But listen, if you would have told me our team, through 10 games, first 10 games of the season, would be 8-2, I'd take it."

stories.title: Winners & Sinners: Week 3
stories.summary: Who and what stood out for the Bucks this week?
stories.detailText: MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 06: Nate Ament #15 of the Milwaukee Bucks blocks the shot of Allen Graves #22 of the Toronto Raptors during the first half of the Emirates NBA Cup Group Play at Fiserv Forum on November 06, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to Winners & Sinners , where we reflect on the week that was for the Milwaukee Bucks. Week 3 saw the Bucks go 0-3, with the team losing to the Minnesota Timberwolves, Boston Celtics, and Toronto Raptors, despite some valiant efforts that put them in positions to win. But who’s deserving of the hardware? MVB Prior to the Raptors game, this was a legitimate conversation between Myles Turner and Tyler Herro. Then Turner pulled one of his all-too-common vanishing acts. Meanwhile, Herro put in his best playmaking performance as a Buck to make it a no contest. And although he’s struggled in first quarters— zero first-quarter points this week—it hasn’t really mattered. He heats up. Quickly. But as Nate O. said in our staff thread, “he’s definitely more than just a microwave—he’s an air fryer.” And so the nickname was born: Tyler Herro, the Air Fryer. Please make this a thing. Defensive Belt Defending Champion : Vacated. The Contenders: Myles Turner, Ryan Rollins. The Decision: I was so ready to anoint Turner as the defensive champion following his showings against the Timberwolves and Celtics, where he was a force blocking shots, accumulating seven across the two games, and also doing yeoman’s work on the boards (at least for him). Then he made it look like the Bucks would have to give up picks in any swap for Jakob Poeltl. Rollins had his moments too, especially when hounding Derrick White. But this belt ain’t no participation award; folks need to take it. And so it’s still collecting dust in the locker room. The People’s Champ This week’s champion is Sausagemahoney, who raised a very thought-provoking question about the Bucks’ decision to take Brayden Burries over Yaxel Lendeborg, who’s since given the zombie Golden State Warriors new life—and who legend Chris Mullin thinks is “going to be a perennial All-Star and just an All-NBA type”: Truthfully, I’m just jealous I didn’t pose the question for this week’s Bucks Reacts Survey . Run That Back If, prior to the season, someone told you that Nate Ament would play fourth-quarter minutes for the Bucks —not the Herd—in the third week of the season, you’d have assumed it would come in garbage time. If they told you he would be a key contributor in a 22-point comeback, splashing an above-the-break three-pointer to cut the lead to two, you’d have called them crazy. Yeah, the Bucks didn’t go on to win this one. And, yes, the Bucks are in the trenches. But moments like this give you a reason to believe. No hesitation, no rim. No ceiling . Not for this rookie. Nate Ament from deep again! pic.twitter.com/lwhllndMFY — Milwaukee Bucks (@Bucks) November 5, 2026 Sinner(s) Whoever coined “Kuzmania” absolutely nailed it—even if it was originally intended as a positive. Like “mania’s” psychiatric denotation, Kyle Kuzma’s game is just all over the place far too often for a tenth-year veteran. This week’s case in point came at the 2:59 mark of the fourth quarter against the Boston Celtics when, after coming back from a 22-point deficit and down only two, Kuzma decides to take a corner three with 19 seconds left on the shot-clock. 19! It wasn’t even as if he was hot—he’d hit only two field goals all game. Of course, after it clanks off rim, the Celtics go on to collect multiple offensive rebounds on the next possession, before Derrick White makes an and-one layup to extend the lead to five. Game over. But the most infuriating thing isn’t even that it cost the Bucks the win, it’s that Kuzma is supposed to be a veteran presence teaching the Bucks’ youth. Some lesson. If… Then… If Taylor Jenkins moving Brayden Burries into the starting lineup is a signpost of his willingness to tinker, then he has to do so elsewhere too. There is absolutely no reason to continue to start Kuzma and play him heavy minutes. None! That’s all for Week 3. Share your winners and sinners in the comments!

stories.title: Jayson Tatum admits Charlotte ‘feels like home’ after NBA Cup masterclass
stories.summary: Tatum was drowned with ‘MVP’ cheers and ‘Let’s go Celtics’ chants in Charlotte on Friday night.
stories.detailText: Nov 6, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Boston Celtics forward Jayson Tatum (0) reacts to his three point basket during the first half against the Charlotte Hornets at Spectrum Center. Mandatory Credit: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Despite being hundreds of miles away from Boston, Jayson Tatum had no trouble feeling at ease in Charlotte, North Carolina, on Friday night. For a moment, the Spectrum Center even began to sound like TD Garden. Chants of ‘Let’s go Celtics’ began filling the arena. In response, the Hornets began turning up the volume on their signature buzzing sound effect in an attempt to drown out the Celtics fans taking over Charlotte. It didn’t work. When Tatum arrived at the free-throw line in the third quarter, he was greeted by a chorus of loud ‘MVP’ chants. “It definitely feels like home,” Tatum confessed after Boston’s 119-80 NBA Cup win, per CLNS Media . Tatum found his footing and began painting his latest masterpiece early on. He scored or assisted on 30 of the Celtics’ first 40 first-quarter points, which tied Paul Pierce for the most 15-point first quarters (106) in the franchise’s play-by-play history, according to ESPN Insights . By halftime, he had reached 24 points on 8-of-14 shooting, including 5-of-8 from beyond the arc, surpassing his combined 3-point makes from his three previous games. JAYSON TATUM GETTING MVP CHANTS IN CHARLOTTE 🗣️ 34 PTS | 8 REB | 9 AST Tatum got checked out from the game after three quarters. pic.twitter.com/nqm2JXrbid — NBA on ESPN (@ESPNNBA) November 7, 2026 If he wanted to, Tatum could’ve pursued his career-high (60 points). But instead, his night was called off after three quarters as the Celtics held a 96-57 runaway lead. At that point, the damage was already done. Tatum only needed three frames to finish with 34 points, eight rebounds, and nine assists, falling a hair shy of securing his first triple-double of the season. He earned a fourth quarter of rest, watching from the bench as head coach Joe Mazzulla allowed reserves including Luka Garza, Mike Conley, and Ron Harper Jr. to get their reps in until the final buzzer. The Celtics found a way to turn a trip to Charlotte into a home-away-from-home experience. For Tatum, as uplifting as the Boston fans in attendance may have been, the 28-year-old had other reasons to feel comfortable in North Carolina, dating back to his teenage years. “I have a lot of connections here in this state, this area,” he explained. “I came here as an 18-year-old kid, my first time spending real time away from home. I was here for a little under a year, and obviously the connection I have here with Duke and the relationships that I’ve been able to build. I always love coming back to North Carolina and love playing here. A lot of Celtics fans, a lot of Duke fans. It’s always a good time coming back.” Throughout his career, Tatum has always flipped the switch in Charlotte. He’s averaged 29.9 points with eight rebounds and 3.7 assists across 15 career games — not including Friday nights — against the Hornets on the road. CHARLOTTE, NC – NOVEMBER 6: Jayson Tatum #0 of the Boston Celtics shoots the ball during the game against the Charlotte Hornets during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on November 6, 2026 at Spectrum Center in Charlotte, North Carolina. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Kent Smith/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images For as many ‘MVP’ chants as Tatum has drawn and will continue to draw this season, this performance certainly lived up to the billing. He did everything. He entered the night shooting 41.8 percent from the field and 22.9 percent from three before going 56.3 percent and 62.5 percent, respectively, in Charlotte. “It was a pretty damn good night,” Payton Pritchard told reporters, per CLNS Media . “34 is pretty good.” Tatum unleashed his dominance, both as a scorer and as a playmaker. He was the undisputed leader, carrying out a belt-to-backside thrashing that took Hornets head coach Charles Lee’s group out of contention well before the game had reached its end. He also got to the line plenty, going a perfect 11-for-11 from the charity stripe. Pritchard continued: “He plays the right way, and he makes great decisions and [he’s] one heck of a ball player for sure.” In each of his first eight appearances this season, Tatum has recorded six-plus assists. It’s been only eight months since Tatum returned from his ruptured Achilles tendon last season, which is much more recent than it might sound. He’s still working toward completing his first full season since returning, and as much as he’s continued to pass the eye test, Tatum still doesn’t consider himself 100 percent just yet. “Hell no,” Tatum told CelticsBlog’s Noa Dalzell . “I wish. I’m getting there, but no. How I felt before I got hurt was really, really good. I don’t feel too far, and again, I still only played less than 40 games since I’ve been back, so still in the quote-unquote rehab phase of returning to play.” Still, he isn’t discouraged by the process. “We’re gonna get there, though,” Tatum added. On Wednesday, the Celtics survived letting go of a 22-point lead against the Milwaukee Bucks as Tatum rested on the sidelines. In Charlotte, they witnessed Tatum make the most of his additional rest and take another step toward becoming the leader Boston will need this season.

stories.title: Luka Doncic's 53-point explosion pushes scoring average past 40 as Lakers roll
stories.summary: Luka Doncic poured in a season-high 53 points in a 124-118 win over the Trail Blazers, raising his scoring average to 40.1 PPG.
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES -- Though Michael Jordan, Kobe Bryant and James Harden came somewhat close, no NBA player has averaged at least 40 points in a season since Wilt Chamberlain in 1962-63. Through his first nine games of the season, Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Doncic is on pace to reach that historic benchmark thanks to his latest 50-point explosion. Doncic poured in a season-high 53 points to lead the Lakers to a 124-118 victory over the Portland Trail Blazers at Crypto.com Arena on Friday. The Slovenian star is averaging a career-high 40.1 points per game as he captains the NBA's No. 1 offense. "Luka can do some things that maybe a handful, if not no one, can do in basketball," Lakers coach JJ Redick said. Chamberlain is the only player to score more than Doncic's 361 points through his first nine games in a season. The Hall of Fame center had 472 points through nine games in 1962-63 and 455 points in the 1961-62 season, according to ESPN Research. Chamberlain went on to average an NBA record 50.4 points in 1961-62 and 44.8 points in 1962-63. Jordan's 37.1 points per game in 1986-87 is the NBA's highest mark during the 3-point era, Harden's 36.1 points per game in 2018-19 was the most prolific scoring season of the 21st century, and Bryant's 35.4 points were the most by a Lakers player since the NBA/ABA merger in 1976. Can Doncic, whose career high for a season is 33.9 points per game with the 2023-24 Dallas Mavericks , join Chamberlain in averaging at least 40 points? "It's obviously a long season," Doncic said. "We're 10 games in. We've got 72 left. As long as we're winning, I'm good. I got [the shots] up today, I'm not going to lie. Hopefully, it continues, but you never know." Doncic, 27, is taking full advantage of his new role as the undisputed face of the Lakers after LeBron James ' offseason departure to the Philadelphia 76ers . Entering Friday, Doncic was leading the league in scoring, shot attempts, 3-point attempts, free throw attempts, usage rate, player efficiency rating and win shares. Against the Trail Blazers, Doncic exceeded 40 points for the sixth time this season and topped 50 for the second time. He ranks tied for 10th all time with 11 career 50-point games and is fifth among active players, trailing only Harden, Stephen Curry , Damian Lillard and James. Doncic, whose 62-foot heave at the halftime buzzer keyed Friday's comeback win, joined Bryant, Elgin Baylor and George Mikan as the only Lakers to score at least 40 points in four consecutive games. "[Doncic] is the MVP right now," Trail Blazers coach Micah Nori said during his pregame comments. "Hands down."

stories.title: Game Preview: Knicks at Cavaliers, November 7, 2026
stories.summary: The Knicks and Cavaliers tangle for an Eastern Conference Finals rematch.
stories.detailText: CLEVELAND, OH - MAY 25: Donovan Mitchell #45 of the Cleveland Cavaliers plays defense on Jalen Brunson #11 of the New York Knicks during Game Four of the 2026 Eastern Conference Finals on May 25, 2026 at Rocket Arena in Cleveland, Ohio. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Nathaniel S. Butler/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Some members from Generation Z might believe that the history of the Cleveland Cavaliers started and ended with a man named LeBron James (not once but twice). They couldn’t be more wrong. The Cavs joined the NBA in 1970 and accumulated plenty of interesting anecdotes through the years, especially early on. For example, they scouted the players for their expansion Draft with the help of trading cards that assistant coach Jim Lessig discovered while shopping for a few gallons of milk. On that understandably subpar inaugural roster was also a man named Gary Suiter, whose biggest contributions were eating hot dogs in the stands during warmups and calling the front office disguised as a fan, lobbying for more playing time for—you guessed it—Gary Suiter. When the well-known bachelor tried to shake down the Cavs for bigger travel expenses by hiring a prostitute to play his wife, even the desperate Cavaliers had enough and kicked him out. Later on, though, basketball really took off in Ohio. The Cavs featured some really exciting teams, especially when the aforementioned James came to town and then came again to actually win a title. Other teams that are fondly remembered in “The Land” are the squads from the late 1980s and 1990s that featured stalwarts like Mark Price, Ron Harper, Brad Daugherty, or Craig Ehlo. Exactly: the guy who is mostly remembered for crumbling to the floor after Michael Jordan’s famous first “shot”, one of the most iconic images in league history. Facing familiar faces on the Cavaliers How history and Cleveland will remember the current iteration of Cavaliers remains to be seen, yet it might very well be decided this year. The headliners on Kenny Atkinson’s team are mostly unchanged from last year’s Eastern Conference Finals sweep at the hands our Knickerbockers. That result could be described as another conquered mountain ledge on the Knicks’ way to the NBA summit, or seen as just another failure by a Cavs’ core that’s been trying to win it all for about three years now. At the heart of that core has been Donovan Mitchell and he is still the headliner at Rocket Arena this season. The stocky highflyer is scoring an efficient 22.5 points per game while probably sporting one of the more explosive games in the league these days. Fans are lamenting his decision making though, criticizing his constant hero ball and what they get for a massive $273 million dollar deal he signed in the summer. Next to Mitchell, a now 37-year-old James Harden runs the point for the Cavaliers, which might also impact “Spida” negatively. The former MVP is showing his age early on, only connects on 38 percent of his shots, and looks disinterested doing it every second night out. THE ENDING OF REGULATION IN CAVS-KNICKS. ABSOLUTE MADNESS. pic.twitter.com/Synu1jsCY5 — Legion Hoops (@LegionHoops) May 20, 2026 Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen still form Cleveland’s frontline—with all their shortcomings, yet also with plenty of talent. The ultra versatile Mobley has taken his physique and his game to another level in recent years, sports a much better jumper from the outside, and the former Defensive Player of the Year isn’t moved off his spots as easily he used to be. If you want a big to switch effortlessly on Jalen Brunson, he’s your man. His current season has been particularly promising with shooting splits of 56/48.6 (we’ll ignore the 63 percent from the line this time around). Allen is kind of there: big, athletic, and skilled, yet you won’t see him in any Strongman or Tough Mudder competitions any time soon. A new supporting cast for Kenny Atkinson After their four starters from last year, Cleveland has mixed it up a bit. They got emerging defensive specialist Peyton Watson from Denver (he is struggling early on with barely 10 points per game), found the talented Meleek Thomas (13.0 points) in the second round of the NBA Draft, and subscribed to the “Super Mario” Hezonja (8.6 points) experience. Sharpshooter Sam Merril and Jaylon Tyson are leftovers from last season and still contribute fairly consistently. Even if Cleveland got a bit longer and a bit more athletic, you still have to wonder where all of this is really going. They are good but how good really? Can they really compete with the top teams in the East? So far there is just a lot of “meh” in their profile. Standing at 5-4 they rank 9th in offensive rating and 14th in defensive rating. They play with a solid yet unspectacular pace (thank you, James Harden) and are average at best on the boards or from the field. Cleveland doesn’t turn the ball over, which is good, yet doesn’t force any turnovers either, which is bad (only the Bucks and Knicks make the opponent cough the ball up fewer times than Cleveland). To be fair, Cleveland is a team that for the most part knows who it is, and such groups can take a little time shaking off the rust, especially after a long last season—we as Bocker buddies know all about it. The Cavaliers, just like the Knicks again, have a lot of things going for them, but it seems like Cleveland unlike New York also has a definitive ceiling. I’d mostly call it James Harden as he has never shown that he can be the ultimate difference maker in the postseason, at least not in a good way. Until then of course the Cavaliers are a perfectly fine, quality opponent, especially at home. They just proved it in their NBA cup last night against the Philadelphia 76ers, dismantling the fighting Nurses 119-95. Let’s hope our Knicks fare a little better tonight and that the biggest historical significance of this game is another win for the good guys. At the very least we don’t have to worry about any of our players binge eating in the stands before the game, I guess. As funny as that would be. stories.summary: A flurry of threes and an unstoppable Tatum led to a full NBA cup win.

(Photo by Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Maybe it was because it was an NBA Cup game. Maybe it was because Jayson Tatum was visiting his old stomping grounds. Maybe it was because the Celtics caught fire from 3. Mix that all together with a few notable absences from the Hornets roster and we got a 119-80 Boston blowout at The Spectrum Center on Friday Night. Why the Celtics won Before being drafted in 2023, Hornets’ Brandon Miller called Paul George his GOAT . You can certainly see the similarities. The lanky 6’9 swingmen are both three level scorers with the biggest difference being the decade-plus between them. Unfortunately, Miller left the game in the second half with a groin soreness with 8 points, a rebound, assist, steal, and block. His idol put up similar numbers. Miller hit just 3-of-10; George was worse at 3-of-11. However, the mutual admiration society doesn’t end there. Tatum once posted back in 2015 when he was at Chaminade that he was “Baby PG” and even boasted that he thinks that he was the first college player to wear the PG1s at Duke. And whenever the Celtics travel down to North Carolina, it’s always going to be a special trip for Tatum. Even though The Hive is 150 miles away from Cameron Indoor Stadium, Tatum just has superpowers playing in Charlotte. Out of the 29 other NBA teams, Tatum averages the most points against the Hornets at nearly 30 per game . And in an NBA Cup game where point differential matters, the defending Player of the Week scored 34 points in just 29 minutes. He was 11-for-11 from the free throw line and 5-of-8 from behind the arc and neared triple-double territory with eight rebounds and nine assists without playing a minute in the fourth quarter. Numbers game: 24 The Celtics flirted with the NBA record for most threes in a game at 29, a feat they tied on Opening Night in 2024 against the Knicks. Boston had 17 at halftime and had it not been a blowout, they might have hit at least five more. Good things come in 3's 👌👌👌 pic.twitter.com/69DkkwQKJt — Boston Celtics (@celtics) November 7, 2026 Instead, they settled for the NBA Cup record at 24 (on 44 attempts). Must C’s Up the eastern seaboard, the Maine Celtics opened their G League season against the Westchester Knicks in blowout fashion as well 123-94. Rookie Dillon Mitchell had six dunks and a triple, including this alley-oop from Milos Uzan. Air Mitchell 🛫 pic.twitter.com/Vxl5kVac3L — Maine Celtics (@MaineCeltics) November 7, 2026 Uzan and Chris Cenac Jr. had 21 a piece in the win. Who said what “Just trying to channel my anger into love.” — head coach Joe Mazzulla to CelticsBlog’s Noa Dalzell on his mid-game hug with Neemias Queta Mazzulla called a timeout because Queta fell down (again) and instead of just yelling at him, he gave him a hug. The Celtics lead the way in their NBA Cup group after their blowout win over the Hornets 🔥 pic.twitter.com/tLH5Ozil1u — Celtics on NBC Sports Boston (@NBCSCeltics) November 7, 2026 After two games, the Celtics are 2-0 with a +53 differential. After the Hawks beat the Wizards 139-132 on Friday night, Boston stands alone at the top of the Eastern Conference’s Group C. They’ll continue this leg of their road-heavy November with a stop in Milwaukee on Sunday and then the marquee face-melter on Tuesday against the 76ers.

stories.title: Letters to Sports: Magical time for Luka Doncic and the Lakers
stories.summary: Readers of the Los Angeles Times Sports section give their thoughts on Luka Doncic, the Lakers, Lincoln Riley, Justin Herbert and more.
stories.detailText: Lakers guards Austin Reaves Luka Doncic celebrate a basket during the first half of a game against the Kings on Wednesday at Sacramento. (Scott Marshall / Associated Press) Luka Doncic has been nothing but extraordinary to start the Lakers’ season. He is hitting shots from all over the court with little or no separation between the defender and himself. The rest of the Lakers are feeding off his energy and playing inspired hoops. And the Lakers are winning! If Luka keeps this up, it will be a season for the ages. We can all thank ex-Mavericks GM Nico Harrison for what might turn out to be the most lopsided trade in the history of professional sports. Dave Ring Manhattan Beach With all his logo threes, and fancy assists, Luka Doncic is the Caitlin Clark of the NBA. Vaughn Hardenberg Westwood Last weekend a letter concluded the only name for a Lakers team that plays hard and entertains every night is “Showtime Lakers.” That nickname belongs to the Laker teams from the 1980s, just like “Phi Slama Jama” belongs to the early 1980s University of Houston basketball team. Regardless of a funny, informal nickname for this season’s Lakers, so far the starting unit has been great fun to watch . Not only has Luka Doncic been on a scoring tear, but Luka has been getting back on defense and even raising his hand when a foul is called on him. Ken Feldman Tarzana Not-so magical I guess Rob Pelinka and JJ Redick forgot that LeBron James is no longer with the Lakers. How else can you explain the waiving of Dalton Knecht and keeping Bronny James. Am I the only one that noticed Bronny was sent down to the G League and Dalton had a successful debut with the Knicks? Stan Shirai Torrance Comparison USC fans have wondered whether Lincoln Riley could measure up to a certain coach across town. After his performance in the Coliseum tunnel and his postgame news conference after the Ohio State game — cursing out Buckeyes’ staffers one minute, reading a prepared statement about “internal joy” the next — we now have our answer: Riley can be every bit as unhinged as Mick Cronin. Wes Wellman Santa Monica Time to change As much as it pains me to say this as a lifelong Chargers fan, please trade Justin Herbert so he can salvage what is left of his once-stellar career (a la Drew Brees). I can no longer bear to watch the countless acknowledged injuries and unacknowledged concussions he sustains each game with this poorly coached team. You are destroying one of the “greatest quarterbacks” in our time. Diane Hom Claremont It’s a coin flip The most intriguing question on the L.A. sports scene remains: Which UCLA Bruins team will be anointed No. 1 in the country first, undefeated footballers or basketballers? Marty Zweben Palos Verdes Estates Greed is not good LIV Golf Chief Executive Officer Scott O’Neil sure served up a heaping helping of atta-boy accolades. Lost in all that, LIV burned through $6 billion in under five years. Mr. O’Neil’s long list of accomplishments is lipstick on the pig. From inception that tour’s financial sensibilities were wack — $100 million, $200 million, $300 million signing bonuses before a stroke was played. Greed killed that beast. David Griffin Westwood Friendly reminder Thank you Bill Dwyre for reminding us that the game is played by the players and not by the announcers. Does Joe Buck deserve $17 million a year, and should Troy Aikman even care, or know how much his partner is making? The guy’s a Hall of Fame quarterback, and as such, should be able to deal with life’s unfairness, if whatever he makes can be considered unfair. Again, this is an insult to the workers, all of them, who barely can make ends meet. Both these guys should be grateful that life is unfair, but not if you’re making millions of dollars for flapping your lips about a game. Ron Brumel West Los Angeles Sure shot When I open my L.A. Times in the morning, I go directly to the sports section and search for Bill Plaschke’s column . I love his style and especially his wit. So he has a prediction miss or two here and there, but no one puts a smile on my face more than him. Keep it up Bill, we all need more laughter in our lives.
