(Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images CLEVELAND — The opposite of love isn’t hate, it’s apathy. LeBron James has gotten many receptions from Cleveland Cavaliers fans over his 24 seasons in the league. None have been as half-hearted and uncarring as Friday’s. There’s always been a certain buzz in the arena when James plays in Cleveland. That has been the case since he was in high school. That juice, however, was lacking in his first trip back home in a Philadelphia 76ers uniform. There were empty seats before tip-off. The ovation for him when he was announced in the starting lineups was positive, but hardly more than respectful . No tribute video was played, as has been the case for the last eight seasons. There were smatterings of boos and cheers throughout the night, but nothing more than what any other high-profile player gets at Rocket Arena. And a good number of fans were content heading out while James was still on the court. In short, LeBron was just another guy participating in one of 41 home games against the Cavs. LeBron James receives a positive reception from Cleveland during player introductions. pic.twitter.com/t4q94ZneSr — Jackson Flickinger (@JacksFlickinger) November 7, 2026 “At this point it’s become normal,” Donovan Mitchell said of James’s return. “My first year, you see it, and now it’s just, we’re playing the Sixers, to be honest. You obviously understand that the stands are going to be packed and obviously cheer for him, and rightfully so. He’s a champion, he’s from here, and he deserves all that and more for what he’s done for the city. At this point it’s just regular. … For us it’s normal.” The normality of this reception stands in stark contrast to what we saw last year . Then, the crowd showered him with praise all game, ultimately moving him to tears . At the time, it seemed unfathomable that he would receive anything but love in the building he called home for 11 years. This summer, however, changed that. James chose to leave the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency at the end of June. He then spent the first three weeks in July dragging his feet, leading those within the city and organization to believe he was returning to Cleveland. But then James threw a curveball and decided to go to a city he had no previous connection with and build a super team with the 76ers. LeBron has earned the right to ring chase at the age of 41. But that comes with consequences, especially when you choose a conference rival over returning to a good team back home that also has a chance of winning a championship. We saw the fallout of that choice on Friday night. There wasn’t the pain and vitriol from 2010. There wasn’t the love in all of his returns since 2018. Just emptiness. LeBron understandably preferred this reaction to what he got when he first returned as a member of the Miami Heat. “Nothing can get as worse as December 2, 2010, from a reception standpoint,” James said. “I’ve seen the end of the depths of hell when it comes to a reception here.” That night in 2010 was an absolute disaster. Cleveland should’ve handled that moment better. They have deserved all of the blame and condemnation that has come from how they handled that. Yet, hate comes from a place of passion. It comes from pain, an emotion that’s real. Fans cared about what happened that night. On Friday, I’m not sure if anyone cared too much anymore. There was appreciation, but there wasn’t undying love. There was frustration, but not enough to actually voice that displeasure. Just a tiredness of a decades-long relationship that keeps oscillating back and forth, without either side really being sure how much they mean to the other. That uncarrying is the saddest place a relationship can find itself, especially one as personal as this. Arguably no professional athlete has meant more to a region than LeBron to Northeast Ohio. The journey from being the teenage prodigy from Akron to delivering the first professional championship in over half a century for a sports-starved region is truly impossible to put into words. The relationship between LeBron and northeast Ohio will continue in some form beyond this. Maybe that appreciation is there if he plays future games in Cleveland. And most likely, that outpouring of love will return for the inevitable statue and jersey retirement ceremonies. But then again, that isn’t guaranteed. James’s choice to presumably end his career in a different uniform could just be the straw that broke the camel’s back. The rift that caused both sides to continue drifting apart forever. Friday could have been LeBron’s last professional game in Northeast Ohio. Nothing about the future is guaranteed. And if so, there couldn’t have been a more pitiful way for things to end in Cleveland.

stories.title: Celtics’ beatdown of Hornets all but guarantees that they’ll advance in the NBA Cup
stories.summary: We want the Cup.
stories.detailText: CHARLOTTE, NC - NOVEMBER 6: Dennis Schroder #17 of the Charlotte Hornets and Jayson Tatum #0 of the Boston Celtics smile after the game during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on November 6, 2026 at Spectrum Center in Charlotte, North Carolina. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Kent Smith/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Friday’s win over the Hornets was every Celtics fans’ dream. Boston took an early lead and instead of letting Charlotte back into the game, they continued put the beatdown on the Hornets until they were up by as many as 46 points. As sick as it is to get a worry-free Celtics win every once in a while, this one hit different. The fact that they were able to dominate an Emirates NBA Cup game like this simply means more — literally. POINT DIFFERENTIAL! pic.twitter.com/hlrZwBdyot — Sam LaFrance (@SamLaFranceNBA) November 7, 2026 Boston sits head and shoulders above Group C now with a perfect 2-0 record and a +53 point differential. That second part is the key. If the first three runs of the Cup taught us anything, it’s that the points matter. If you remember, the standings are decided by record, then head-to-head record, and then point differential. Anytime there’s a three-way tie, it goes straight to the points. Boston is in full control of their fate at this point. Win their remaining games, and they’ll move onto the knockout stage — it’s that simple. As well all know, though, it isn’t always that easy with the Cs. In fact, they’ve never swept group play in the tournament. They love to lay an egg in some game that they have no business losing. Their remaining matchups in the group are against the most formiddable teams — the Wizards and Hawks. These are two games Boston should win, but again, nothing is guaranteed. In that case, we’re all thinking about points again. If the best record in Group C is 3-1, then Boston could still win the group. But if it’s solely on head-to-head record, the other 3-1 team would likely be the one that beat them. So… the Wild Card would be their only path forward. After going down to Charlotte and bringing 48 minutes of pain to the hosts, the Cs hold the best point-differential in the Eastern Conference. The Cavaliers (+24), Heat (+20), and Pistons (+16) are the only other teams who are positive double-digits. Granted, most teams have only played one Cup game, so they’ll have an extra chance to make up ground in that area. But Boston is looking good for now. All of this is to say that as long as the Celtics win one more Cup game and don’t lose by a billion if they do drop one, then they should be on track to keep climbing towards their first ever deep run in the competition. Frankly, if they don’t advance, it’ll be extremely disappointing. As much as some fans don’t care for colorful courts and shenanigans that come with the Cup, it does add a lot of flare to these November nights and half a million bucks into the pockets of the players. Plus, if the Celtics are in a competition, you should want them to win every single time. The more trophies the franchise collects, the better.

stories.title: Swanson: Luka Doncic can lead Lakers to a title, but only if his teammates pull their weight
stories.summary: The Lakers' superstar is on an MVP pace like few others before, but to win an NBA title he has to have sustainability that his teammates must help him attain.
stories.detailText: Guards Austin Reaves and Luka Doncic celebrate in the final seconds of the Lakers' over the Trail Blazers in an NBA Cup group game on Friday night at Crypto.com Arena. (Gina Ferazzi / Los Angeles Times) Luka Doncic is hooping like he intends to run away with the MVP trophy. Making a point by scoring more points to start a season — 361 in nine games — than anyone since Wilt Chamberlain scored 472 in 1962. Generational scoring run or the new normal? Could this historic meteor shower be the standard? “I feel like that,” Doncic said, adding he thinks he can maintain his current 40.1-points-per-game tear. “But as long as we win, I’m good.” And if he’s this good when the playoffs roll around, this undeniable, brushing off elite defenders Toumani Camara and Jrue Holiday en route to 53 points in Friday’s 124-118 victory over the Portland Trail Blazers, then the Lakers could totally go on a Luka Magical run and win it all. But if Doncic is not this good, the Lakers aren’t 8-2 right now, and they’re not sitting in first in the Western Conference standings out of the gate … with 72 more games to go. There’s ability, there’s inevitability, bankability. Read more: Luka Doncic scores 53 as Lakers avenge loss to Trail Blazers And then there’s sustainability. The Lakers are going to need to employ some serious conservation measures to get this version of Doncic — whose seven consecutive 35-points-or-better games put him on par with Elgin Baylor and Kobe Bryant as the only Lakers to stack so many in regular-season history — to the starting line that matters. They need to write to Santa Claus and ask for a serviceable backup center. They need Austin Reaves to really rock and roll with the units that don’t include Doncic — who has the highest plus-minus and the highest on/off rating in the NBA — and to keep his turnover tallies low. They need to not just beat but blow out bad teams, to give Doncic a fourth quarter off sometimes. And they need coach JJ Redick — who boasted in September that the Lakers’ “naturally deeper roster” would result in a longer rotation — to trust the process. Even if the amount of “my bad” from his backups costs the Lakers some regular-season wins, it will, on occasion, make more sense to punt than to go for it. Like when you’re readying a less-experienced, less-familiar team for future battles. And wanting to reduce wear and tear on your engine. A proven power-lifter, the 27-year-old Doncic is this season handling the heaviest workload (39.8% usage rate) in the NBA and in his career, while logging 35.9 taxing minutes per game. Lakers guard Luka Doncic reacts after sinking a three-point shot to give the Lakers a five-point lead against the Trail Blazers in the third quarter Friday night at Crypto.com Arena. (Gina Ferazzi / Los Angeles Times) He’s being challenged, pressed and trapped. He’s accelerating and decelerating and accelerating again. He’s charge-taking, pump-faking, piling up hoops-and-harms. Manipulating defenses and defending like he’s taken some slander personally. Arguing with officials and heaving vibey buzzer-beaters from all over the building, including a 61-footer that completely altered the complexion of Friday’s game, giving the Lakers momentum for the first time entering intermission. And, no, he doesn’t need to play heavy minutes to prepare to play heavy minutes in the playoffs. He also doesn’t need to be wrapped in bubble wrap, but ideally he’d ramp up for the anchor leg instead of sprinting for the full marathon. Remember what happened last season, after Doncic set the league on fire in March, averaging 37.5 points per game as the Lakers went 15-2 and announced themselves as challengers? He suffered a Grade 2 hamstring strain on April 2 that sidelined him for the rest of the season and doused the Lakers’ hopes. And look around now; the league is a cautionary tale of the tape. Anthony Edwards, Chet Holmgren, Ja Morant, Tyrese Haliburton, Jalen Williams are among the stars who’ve been lost to injuries. The Lakers — who are starting the season by playing three weeks without a single two-day break between games — don’t want to be included in the discussion about what’s ailing the NBA’s highest-usage talent this season. It might be that the game has evolved to become more grueling, that teams are averaging more possessions per game, that possessions are shorter and that defenders are picking up ball-handlers sooner. But it’s not, Portland coach Micah Nori said, because guys aren’t in shape: “They all have individual trainers, and they all work extremely hard, and they put in a lot of time — essentially 12 months out of the year. Back in the day, no disrespect to those guys, but that’s why training camp was so long, because they needed training camp to get back in shape. And so now they’re never out of shape, and I don’t know if that has any bearing … but that’s the only difference I see. That includes Doncic. “He is the best shape I’ve ever seen him in,” Nori said, proclaiming the Lakers’ star his (way-too-early) favorite for MVP. Forget about that, though. Shohei Ohtani being dead set on chasing the Cy Young Award killed the Dodgers’ chances at a three-peat. And Doncic doing too much and earning his first MVP honor wouldn’t do anything for the Lakers’ championship chances if he’s spent by the time the postseason starts. He’s much too valuable for that. Sign up for our weekly newsletter on all things Lakers. This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

stories.title: Former Cavs forward Dean Wade expected to be back in Cleveland this season
stories.summary: Wade says he originally planned on returning to Cleveland.
stories.detailText: CLEVELAND, OHIO - NOVEMBER 06: Donovan Mitchell #45 of the Cleveland Cavaliers drives to the basket against Dean Wade #45 of the Philadelphia 76ers during the second half at Rocket Arena on November 06, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Cavaliers , like a few other teams, found themselves completely preoccupied this summer with courting LeBron James. In the process, they were unwilling or unable to give Dean Wade a financial commitment. “I kind of thought I’d probably just come back,” Wade said after playing his first game in Cleveland this season. “Unfortunately, that didn’t happen.” Perhaps the Cavs would have elected to move on from Wade either way. He had run his course in Cleveland, and the Cavs clearly wanted to find an upgrade at small forward. That’s certainly part of the equation. But it also seems possible that Cleveland was holding out for LeBron — and Wade leaving was a product of that waiting game. Regardless of how it happened, Wade says he’s happy with the end result. “Philly’s awesome, this team is always great, high-character people,” said Wade. “It’s weird going to a new place with me, like 1,000 new faces and stuff. But after a couple of weeks, it gets a lot easier. So I’m pretty happy with my decision.” Support us and Let ‘Em Know with Homage! Anything bought from the links helps support Fear the Sword . You can buy the Believeland shirt HERE . You can also shop all of Homage’s Cavs gear HERE . Wade played seven seasons with the Cavaliers, going from an undrafted prospect in 2019 to a starter in the playoffs. This was his first time entering Rocket Arena as an enemy. “It was weird; emotions were high, and it was pretty hard to stay focused,” said Wade. “But it was good. I was happy to see everybody.” The Cavs leaned on Wade for his defense throughout the last seven seasons. But his progression from a fringe NBA player to a legitimate rotational piece is worth remembering. He’s a developmental success story that helped bolster the Cavs for nearly a decade. “Above all, you loved the person, loved the family; they’re just incredible,” Cavs coach Kenny Atkinson said of Wade. “Great for our culture, obviously the player, he’s a heck of a player, helped us a lot even before I got here, a major player for the team — happy he landed in a good spot.” Wade is now playing a similar role in Philly, while the Cavs are hoping Peyton Watson will be everything they’ve needed at small forward. It’s a breakup that has zero hard feelings on either end.

stories.title: Observations after Sixers suffer blowout loss to Cavs, fall in NBA Cup
stories.summary: The Sixers fell to their second loss of the season on Friday night in Cleveland.
stories.detailText: Observations after Sixers suffer blowout loss to Cavs, fall in NBA Cup originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers couldn’t rekindle the magic of their comeback home-opening win over the Cavaliers. They fell Friday night in NBA Cup action, suffering a 119-95 defeat in Cleveland. The Sixers dipped to 8-2 and the Cavs improved to 5-4. The Sixers’ top scorers were Jaylen Brown (20 points), VJ Edgecombe (19 points) and Tyrese Maxey (17). The Cavs got 23 points from Donovan Mitchell and 22 from Evan Mobley. The Sixers’ injured players included center Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain). Cleveland was down big man Jarrett Allen (right knee contusion). Sam Merrill sat out the second half with a right elbow injury. With Friday’s loss, the Sixers are 1-1 in Eastern Conference Group B of the NBA Cup. Their next Cup game is scheduled for Nov. 25 against the Heat. The Sixers will conclude their three-road trip Sunday afternoon against the Bulls. Here are observations on their blowout loss to Cleveland: Nightmare start for Embiid, Sixers After a missed Merrill three-pointer, the Sixers steamed ahead on the fast break and Edgecombe opened the scoring with a slam. The Cavs replied with a 15-0 run kickstarted by six straight Mitchell points. Much like in the Sixers’ Oct. 22 win over Cleveland , they were many levels below their best in the first quarter. The Sixers began 0 for 4 from three-point range, including two LeBron James misses. The Cavs were also the better team in transition and limited the Sixers’ chances to attack in the open floor by taking excellent care of the ball in the early going. Edgecombe was called for his second foul with 7:34 left in the first quarter. Meanwhile, Joel Embiid expressed his frustration about a couple of early no-calls. Embiid’s larger problem was that he couldn’t hit any sort of shot besides free throws. He went 0 for 9 from the floor in the game. The seven-time All-Star finished with six points and seven rebounds. Embiid has had a subpar shooting start to the year, especially from three-point territory — he’s now 3 for 28 (10.7 percent) — but Friday was the kind of extreme night that’s bound to happen here and there over the course of a long season. Of course, it’s notable that Embiid’s been playing through right foot plantar fasciitis and the Sixers have been keeping a close eye on his minutes. We’ll see how the team manages his availability moving forward and whether Embiid is able to bounce back next time out. James didn’t play anywhere near his finest game either. He had eight points on 3-for-12 shooting, eight rebounds, three assists and six turnovers. As a team, the Sixers were 36.5 percent from the field and 25 percent beyond the arc. Edgecombe shrugs off foul trouble Jabari Walker rejoined the Sixers’ rotation as the backup center with Bona sidelined. Anfernee Simons, former Cav Dean Wade and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope all remained rotation fixtures. With Walker and Caldwell-Pope on the court next to three starters, the Sixers cut their deficit to single digits in the second quarter. Walker threw down a fast-break dunk that cut Cleveland’s lead to 48-41. He gave the Sixers some good defensive possessions when switched on to James Harden and provided his usual physical, high-effort work on the glass. Edgecombe was fantastic in the second, sinking three triples, racking up 15 points and nabbing three steals. Many second-year players would have a tough time finding a rhythm after encountering early foul trouble, but Edgecombe was great as soon as he checked back in and delivered a ton of valuable buckets in the Sixers’ comeback push. Cavs polish it off in 2nd half The Sixers pulled to within 66-63 when Maxey picked a steal and threw a pretty one-handed bounce pass to Edgecombe for a dunk. With Embiid and James offering little as scorers, Brown hit several shots that helped the Sixers stay in the game. After his 30-point performance last time out against the Pistons , Brown reached the 20-point mark for a third consecutive game. Still, the Sixers’ offense never got rolling. The Cavs maintained their lead and extended it late in the third quarter. By early in the fourth, the Sixers trailed by over 20 points. Embiid didn’t play the fourth quarter and logged 25 minutes. He’s had zero made field goals on just one other occasion in his career , back in Nov. 2019 against the Raptors. Even with their tremendous first nine games, the Sixers knew they’d hit speed bumps throughout the year. They’ll try to get back on track Sunday in Chicago.

stories.title: LeBron James is having fun in Philly and one fan's wine can prove it
stories.summary: LeBron James took fan interaction to a whole new level on Monday night.
stories.detailText: LeBron James is having fun in Philly and one fan's wine can prove it originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia LeBron James is one of kind in so many ways. What he did Monday night might be the cherry on top. In the third quarter of the Sixers’ 126-107 victory over the Bulls, James decided he’d take fan interaction to a whole new level. He helped himself to a fan’s red wine. James looked for a transition pass from Tyrese Maxey, who snagged a rebound. James was behind the pass and his momentum took him into the stands, where he disappeared for a few moments. It wasn’t until another angle was shown on replay that we could see what actually went down in the darkness of the seats. James didn’t hold back giving reporters a play-by-play. “I spilled some of his wine,” he said postgame. “I crashed into him, spilled some of his wine. So I wanted to see if it was worth it on my arm and how good it was. It was alright.” Troy Clemons – the Sixers fan whose drink spilled – explained his perspective on the interaction with James to Kris Rhim of ESPN. “[I was] walking to my seat … LeBron crashed into me, he grabbed me, he said ‘My bad,’ my drink spilled everywhere. He took my drink from me and he basically just took a sip of it, gave it back and ran back on the [court].” Did he keep the cup? “At the end of the day he’s another man like me,” Clemons said. “I mean he’s LeBron, but at the end of the day, I threw that cup in the trash. And it’s nothing up with him, I just got a fresh drink though.” It should be noted that players are not supposed to drink from fans’ cups, but it’s rare for the NBA to fine someone for a spontaneous interaction such as this. In 2019, a similar thing happened when Mike Scott tumbled into the Bucks’ court-side seats. The Sixers star jokingly took a sip of a fan’s beverage and the NBA opted not to fine him. Time will tell if James has the same fate. If nothing else, an interaction like this just shows how much fun James seems to be having. The 24-year veteran noted the importance of finding joy in the game as he grinds through the season. “It’s a long marathon. And if you don’t find ways to have fun throughout it, even though you’re working and even though you’re locked in, then it could wear on you. So for me, especially at this point in my career, being able to just appreciate the moments, the small moments, these fans are great to us. We try to be great to them as well. By playing the game the right way, playing the game hard and then also just being showmen as well, it was a great game for us.” Head coach Nick Nurse also weighed in on the 41-year-old’s mindset coming into the season. “This summer I think he probably stated publicly that he wanted to go some place and have some fun playing. He loves the game, [it’s his] 24th year. It’s a group of guys, like I keep saying, that have been super focused in the intent of playing the right way. I think he’s a big part of that.” The vibes are high. It’s difficult for them not to be. With Monday’s win against the Bulls, the Sixers are 7-1 and lead the Eastern Conference. They’ve won four in a row and the only team they’ve lost to is the Pistons. The Sixers will face them on Wednesday to start a three-game road trip.

stories.title: Observations after Sixers earn strong road win over Pistons, Brown scores 30
stories.summary: Jaylen Brown's 30-point night helped the 8-1 Sixers top the Pistons.
stories.detailText: Observations after Sixers earn strong road win over Pistons, Brown scores 30 originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers remain the Eastern Conference’s sole leader. They earned a 112-106 road win over the Pistons on Wednesday night to move to 8-1 on the season and stay at the top of the standings. Detroit fell to 6-2. The Sixers last started 8-1 in the 2023-24 season, which was Nick Nurse’s first as the team’s head coach. Jaylen Brown scored a season-high 30 points and pulled down seven rebounds. Joel Embiid had 26 points and a season-best 15 rebounds. LeBron James posted 13 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists. Tyrese Maxey added 19 points and seven assists. The Pistons’ leading scorers were Duncan Robinson with 27 points and Cade Cunningham with 26. The Sixers were down Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear). The Pistons’ injured players included Jalen Duren (right hamstring strain) and Isaiah Joe (right hip contusion). Nurse told reporters in Detroit he thinks “it’ll be another 10 to 12 days before they kind of clear (Barlow) for getting on the court to see where he is,” according to Sixers Wire’s Ky Carlin. The Sixers will visit the Cavaliers on Friday night. Here are observations on their victory over Detroit: Little bit of everything from Embiid in 1st half Embiid assisted the Sixers’ first basket with a sharp pass out of a double team. He saw Brown’s cut along the baseline and dished to him for a layup. Detroit ran several double drag screen actions early, forcing Embiid to defend on the perimeter. The Pistons started 7 for 11 from the floor and took a 17-11 edge on a Robinson three-pointer. The Sixers then made a 10-0 run and Embiid was right in the middle of it. He converted a put-back layup after a pretty high-low feed from James. Embiid hit two foul shots to give the Sixers the lead. The team raised its defensive level and Detroit’s offense grew frigid. Embiid was very good on the glass in the first half, grabbing eight rebounds. The Sixers had an excellent rebounding game as a team, limiting the Pistons to four offensive boards over 48 minutes. Embiid didn’t break out of his early-season three-point shooting slump, going 0 for 3. He’s 3 for 26 (11.5 percent) on the season and hasn’t made a three since the Sixers’ second game. Late in the second quarter, Embiid got into a dead-ball dust-up with Tolu Smith. After an officials’ review, Embiid was assessed a technical foul for “initiating” the altercation. Brown steps up Playing on his 26th birthday, Maxey missed his first four field goals and was scoreless until he hit a floater with 31.5 seconds left in the first quarter. Brown picked up the scoring slack, tallying 10 points in the first on 4-for-6 shooting and hitting a deep, buzzer-beating three to put the Sixers up 29-21. He produced at all three levels, chose smart spots to attack and looked comfortable in the rhythm of the Sixers’ offense. Meanwhile, James did his usuall stellar work as a passer. He assisted two Adem Bona slams in the second quarter and constantly spotted open teammates. Nurse rewarded Bona’s strong opening stint, playing him for a lengthy stretch. Brown swished a corner triple to extend the Sixers’ lead to 48-31. With a 3-for-5 night, Brown is at 45.7 percent from long distance so far this season. It wouldn’t be surprising at all if Brown’s three-point shooting improved from last season’s 34.7 percent clip. With such an abundance of star power, the Sixers’ hope will be that everyone gets regular open looks beyond the arc throughout the year. As for Maxey, he sat with 3:26 left in the second quarter after being whistled for his third foul. Even with a mere two points from Maxey, the Sixers entered halftime holding a 14-point advantage. Sixers stay perfect away from home The Pistons played better basketball to begin the third quarter. Following a John Collins alley-oop jam, Nurse called timeout with his team’s lead down to single digits. The Pistons’ offense sustained some success, but the Sixers prevented a sustained run. Embiid played an especially physical, aggressive third quarter. He tipped in his own miss and Maxey then sunk a three to make the Sixers’ lead 84-68. They were up as many as 17 points in the third. Embiid sat out the fourth quarter Monday night for the Sixers’ win over the Bulls and said he was on a minutes restriction (25) because of his right foot plantar fasciitis. He played the fourth period against the Pistons and logged 33 minutes. Bona went back to the locker room early in the fourth. Nurse told reporters postgame that Bona had “neck soreness.” Detroit did not let the Sixers coast to victory. Robinson drained a three. Cunningham made a pair of free throws and drove in for a layup that cut the Pistons’ deficit to 106-102. The Sixers halted the Pistons’ run before anything disastrous was on the table. Brown blocked a Cunningham three-point try, Embiid knocked down two foul shots, and the East’s No. 1 early-season team improved to 4-0 on the road.

stories.title: ‘I'm finding my footing': Jaylen Brown's role taking shape with Sixers
stories.summary: Brown is complementing Philadelphia’s stars, attacking the glass and setting a "non-negotiable" defensive standard during the Sixers’ 7-1 start.
stories.detailText: ‘I'm finding my footing': Jaylen Brown's role taking shape with Sixers originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia Jaylen Brown has spent the opening weeks of the season describing the Sixers as a work in progress. He offered a similarly humble perspective Monday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena. His performance, however, provided the clearest look yet at how he can influence this group while sharing the floor with the club’s other established stars. Brown finished with 25 points, 11 rebounds and five assists in the Sixers’ 126-107 win over the Chicago Bulls. He shot 9 for 15 from the field, made four three-pointers and did not commit a turnover. Five of his rebounds came on the offensive end, an area Brown has emphasized while the Sixers continue piecing together their frontcourt rotation. “Just a mindset,” Brown said. “Just trying to create extra opportunities for my team. As we’re trying to patch together our fives and our front line, I try to make an extra contribution and emphasis on the glass.” Brown has also been careful about how he describes his place on a roster that already belonged to Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey. Maxey scored 15 of his 26 points in the fourth quarter Monday, continuing his torrid start to the season. He has led the Sixers in scoring while being the only starter to appear in all eight games. Brown is not interested in interrupting that. “Maxey’s been leading the way, 100 percent,” Brown said. “He’s been here. This is his team. Him and Joel have been here for a while, so the mindset has been to complement those guys. I’m finding my footing, but Maxey has been leading the way for sure.” Brown’s footing looked firm against Chicago. Beyond his scoring, he helped the Sixers control the glass, moved the ball within an offense that generated 23 assists during the first half and supplied the physicality Nick Nurse expects from him. “The dude is tough and he wins,” Nurse said. “I’ll take that all day long. The degree of difficulty on some of the shots he hit was really amazing. I thought he pounded the glass and got some key rebounds. Makes a lot of winning plays. Man, he’s a winner.” Brown spent the first 10 years of his career in Boston. He won a championship there, reached another NBA Finals and grew from a 20-year-old prospect into one of the league’s premier two-way wings. Moving into a new system alongside James, Embiid and Maxey was never going to be seamless. “I mean, he’s fitting in along with all of us,” James said. “We’re getting better and better. It’s not going to happen overnight. He spent his first 10 years in a system in Boston, in the city, so it’s going to take some adjustment. “It takes adjustment for him. It’s going to take adjustment for the rest of the guys that joined this franchise as well. But tonight was a great step.” James pointed to Brown’s “pressure, his shot-making ability, his rebounding ability” and his professionalism. Brown’s early influence has extended beyond his production. The Sixers entered Monday with one of the NBA’s best half-court defenses. Brown has been one of the group’s most persistent voices, stressing communication, preparation and attention to opposing players’ tendencies. “That’s the part that I care about the most as a group, not individually,” Brown said. “Having a mentality night in and night out, respecting your opponent, respecting the game, making sure that we are executing our coverages, we’re being clear in our communication and then we’re also taking away tendencies on a night-to-night basis. “Those things I just explained are over 50 percent of the battle.” Brown understands that maintaining those details across an 82-game schedule will require more than reminders. “A little bit of accountability,” he said. “You learn different guys require different things. How you communicate with each guy may be a little different, but accountability for sure and confrontation if need be. “The offense is going to be what it’s going to be, but our defense has got to be non-negotiable. That’s something I say all the time. Non-negotiable. You want to be a good team, defense is non-negotiable.” The Sixers showed both sides of their defensive potential Monday. They built a double-digit lead during the first half, allowed Chicago to score 36 points in the second quarter and then created separation after halftime. Philadelphia held the Bulls to 20 points in the third quarter before pulling away in the fourth. Brown did not celebrate their ability to raise their intensity after it slipped. “I don’t like that we have that,” he said. “It’s good that we have shown the potential, but we’ve got to keep that switch on. It doesn’t work like that where you just flip the switch. “It can catch up to us and it can bite us against a better team or on a night that we’re not being as crisp on offense. It can’t be a switch just because we’re playing a lesser opponent or whatever the case may be. We’ve got to make sure that mentality is from the beginning to end. Can’t skip any steps.” That urgency accompanies considerable optimism. Brown said the Sixers enjoy playing together. He loves when James grabs a rebound because “he’s like a quarterback,” capable of launching an outlet pass or immediately pushing the pace. The group is learning when to attack, when to move the ball and how to avoid hesitating in its effort to play unselfishly. “It’s a lot of talent, man,” Brown said. “We like each other, and we’re just kind of building that chemistry of how we can get this thing to a well-oiled machine. I think we’re taking steps forward every single day.” The Sixers are 7-1 despite Brown believing those steps remain incomplete. They have won close games, erased sizable deficits and received important contributions from different players. Brown’s performance Monday showed another version of how their pieces can fit. “We still have a long way to go to being a really, really solid, great team,” Brown said. “But we’ve been able to win some games. We started out the season great, 7-1, and you haven’t seen our best version yet. “That’s a good sign.”

stories.title: Observations after Sixers beat Bulls to reach East-leading 7-1
stories.summary: The Sixers stayed hot Monday night, reaching 7-1 with a win over the Bulls.
stories.detailText: Observations after Sixers beat Bulls to reach East-leading 7-1 originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers kept up their hot start to the season Monday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, reaching 7-1 with a 126-107 win against the Bulls. All five of the Sixers’ starters scored in double figures. Tyrese Maxey posted 26 points on 10-for-15 shooting and 11 assists. Jaylen Brown tallied a season-best 25 points and 11 rebounds. VJ Edgecombe’s 21 points were a new season high. LeBron James recorded 15 points, nine assists and seven boards. Bulls rookie Caleb Wilson had 24 points and seven rebounds. Joel Embiid (15 points, eight rebounds) had been listed as questionable with an official designation of “right foot plantar fascia injury management.” He sat out Saturday on the second night of a back-to-back for the Sixers’ win over the Hornets. “Plantar is a little bit of a come and go type of thing,” Sixers head coach Nick Nurse told reporters pregame. “They’re just trying to manage it. It’s very painful, if you’ve ever had it. It can kind of come and go out of nowhere. So we’re just trying to manage the pain with that, be as smart as we can.” Nurse told reporters that Dominick Barlow is set to see a specialist Tuesday about the back injury that’s sidelined him to start the season. “He’s been on court a little bit … not a ton of moving around,” Nurse said. “I think they want to get to tomorrow’s appointment. Hopefully, it’ll be positive and we can get into his workouts a little bit.” The Sixers will begin a three-game road trip Wednesday when they visit the Pistons. Here are observations on their victory Monday: Edgecombe slamming away off the bat After Embiid blitzed a Bulls pick-and-roll, Maxey picked off Matas Buzelis’ hurried pass to get the Sixers rolling in transition and James jammed home the team’s first field goal. Edgecombe got a slam soon after James grabbed a defensive rebound and the Sixers again pushed the pace. The Sixers scored six quick fast-break points, leading the Bulls to burn an early timeout, and James’ long-distance feeds were a major asset. “If you’re open, he’s going to pass it,” Edgecombe said of James. “The main thing is just being ready. Tonight I had to run and go get ‘em. If you’re open and he sees you, he’s going to pass the ball.” Edgecombe had a dunk-heavy first quarter. He threw down his second when Dean Wade nabbed a steal and dropped off a typically selfless dish to the Sixers’ explosive second-year guard, whose slam put the team up 22-13. The Sixers have an abundance of dangerous options in the open floor, Edgecombe included. As he’s already shown with his continued clutch shotmaking, the 21-year-old won’t become anything resembling a non-factor offensively this year as a byproduct of the Sixers’ enhanced star power. Over the team’s first seven games, Edgecombe had averaged 11.3 points. He scored 11 in the first period on 5-for-5 shooting. More rough minutes for Bona Adem Bona missed a dunk early in the second quarter, which stung a bit more when Jalen Smith drilled a three-pointer seconds later. Bona remained the Sixers’ main backup center. He had a poor first-half stint overall amid a largely negative start to his third season. The 23-year-old big man played well in the Sixers’ victory over the Bucks , posting six points, 13 rebounds and three blocks. Outside of that, his season has been sparse on bright moments so far. It’s reasonable to wonder when Nurse might turn to alternatives like Jabari Walker, who played a good game Saturday in Charlotte, or try James again at the five. The Bulls outscored the Sixers by eight points in Bona’s first run, cutting their derficit to 40-38. Chicago went in front with a three by former Sixer Buddy Hield. The Sixers regained the advantage late in the second quarter. Maxey and James each were excellent as passers in the first half, combining for 14 assists and three turnovers. James fired the ball to Wade for a corner three that gave the Sixers a 60-52 lead. Sixers outclass Bulls Following a third-quarter Embiid fadeaway jumper and two James lay-ins, the Sixers were up 17 points. The Bulls cut the Sixers’ lead down to 11 points by the start of the fourth quarter. With Bona still struggling and on four fouls, Wade began the fourth at center. Bona then briefly spelled Wade before being whistled for his fifth foul and taking a seat. Embiid ultimately wasn’t needed for any of the fourth period and only logged 25 minutes. Embiid said postgame that he was not available to return to the action in the fourth and has been feeling his plantar fasciitis on the court. The seven-time All-Star’s health is clearly not close to 100 percent. “I was on a minutes restriction,” he said. “(The foot) has been going like that for the past few weeks. It’s painful. Just got to manage it. “If it flares up pretty bad, got to take a step back. We’ve been able to manage it, but it has its ups and downs.” The Sixers’ lead got as low as eight points, but Chicago did not shoot well enough from three-point range (26.3 percent) or have sufficient firepower to sustain a meaningful comeback run. The bottom line is the Sixers are in a different class than the Bulls, who fell to 1-6. As for the Sixers, they’ll wake up Tuesday morning at the top of the Eastern Conference standings. “You’ve got some of these nights where you kind of call them professional wins. …You look at the records and all that kind of stuff, but they have a lot of talent,” Nurse said. “A lot of these teams play a way that’s a little scary. It’s fast and it’s furious, lots of threes. … They’re going to keep coming at you, high-possession games. So they’re not easy games and I’m glad that we handled it professionally tonight.”

teamStories.detailText: SACRAMENTO, CA - NOVEMBER 6: Dylan Harper #2 of the San Antonio Spurs drives to the basket during the game against the Sacramento Kings during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on November 6, 2026 at Golden 1 Center in Sacramento, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Rocky Widner/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Before the season and even into the first few games, critics have questioned the San Antonio Spurs’ four-guard starting lineup. However, through 9 games, that lineup has a +25.4 net rating in 95 minutes and has led the Spurs to a 7-2 start. The bench lineups, especially those without Victor Wembanyama, have caused the team issues. That was never more apparent than in San Antonio’s 124-109 thrashing of the Sacramento Kings on Friday night. Let’s be honest about the Kings for a moment. They are a bad basketball team, perhaps not in talent, but in discipline and execution. They lose people on defense and take errant shots on offense. Yet, multiple times on Friday, they gained back ground with most of San Antonio’s starters off the floor. Most of San Antonio’s mistakes come from defense, where too often players, especially on the wings, overhelp on a drive or watch the ball, letting the offensive player get an open three or cut to the rim and score over the top of Luke Kornet. San Antonio’s defensive lapses were a big reason the Kings shot 49% from the field and hit 46% from three. That second unit’s defensive issues don’t flip the game against the worst in the league, but against a legitimate, deep team, it could lead to a loss. The Spurs will take a 15-point win on the road in their first NBA Cup game. But it’s hard to come out of that game feeling overly confident about the performance. San Antonio has won seven games in a row, but over half of those have come against teams under .500. A real test awaits them on Saturday in the red-hot Portland Trail Blazers. The Spurs’ second unit will need to step up its defensive play if they want to compete with another Western Conference leader. Takeaways: Devin Vassell is one of the most important players on the Spurs. Vassell is shooting 34.1% from three this season, well below his usual average, which has hurt San Antonio’s offense. When he’s hitting shots, like he did against Sacramento, the offense opens up a ton for the guards and Wembanyama to dominate the paint. Vassell had 19 points, hitting 5 of his 6 threes on Friday. His off-ball defense was solid, too. He did about all you can ask from a glue guy in the starting lineup. San Antonio will need more performances like these moving forward. The Kings ran one of the weakest zones I’ve seen this season, and it led to a big run from the Spurs in the first half. That said, it made me realize that San Antonio is basically built to bust zone defenses. One, Wembanyama is kind of the ultimate cheat code to beat a zone. He can stretch it out on the perimeter or punish smaller players who get caught helping around the basket in the zone. Then, the Spurs have dynamic playmaking guards who are big and physical and can operate in the middle of the zone, a common weak spot in many zone defenses. Add in a couple of knockdown shooters like Vassell and Champagnie, and it becomes nearly impossible to run zone against San Antonio. The Kings tried, and failed to do so on Friday. Stephon Castle had a rough defensive night, but made up for it with some of the best playmaking we’ve seen from him this season. He had 19 points, 7 assists, and 1 turnover in the win. One of those assists came on a beautiful inverted pick-and-roll with Wembanyama as the ball handler and Castle as the screener. Castle caught the ball on the short roll, did a 180-degree turn, and fired the ball to a wide-open Vassell for three. It was as close to the Beautiful Game Spurs as San Antonio got on Friday. Harrison Barnes has earned his spot in the rotation lately, and one could argue he should be getting more minutes than some other bench forward on the roster. He had 13 points on 4-for-7 shooting on Friday against his former team. Offensively, he’s a savvy connective player who can take advantage of a defense that is out of position after one of the Spurs’ guards creates an advantage. He looks more like the Barnes we saw in his first season with San Antonio, rather than last year. He has essentially replaced Carter Bryant in the rotation, and it doesn’t look like he will be giving up that spot any time soon with how he is playing. I’m interested to see how this team will look once Tobias Harris comes back (hopefully this month?). They desperately need another shot creator and capable defender in that second unit. I know a lot of people want to see him replace Vassell in the starting lineup, but it seems like he could provide even more value as one of the first subs in the game, then playing for a prolonged stretch alongside Kornet and one or two of the guards. The Spurs’ top free-agent acquisition should give them more of the versatility many thought the team would have going into the season.

stories.title: Vikings WR Jauan Jennings on rebuffing return to 49ers: 'I love where I'm at'
stories.summary: Jauan Jennings said he rebuffed the chance to return to the 49ers via trade despite struggling to produce for the Vikings because "I love where I'm at."
stories.detailText: EAGAN, Minn. -- Jauan Jennings explained Saturday why he voiced a desire to remain with the Minnesota Vikings earlier this season, despite a steep production decline, as the team discussed a trade that would have returned him to the San Francisco 49ers , where he played the first six seasons of his career. "I just thought it was best for both teams," Jennings told ESPN. "No distractions. I love where I'm at." Jennings, who signed a one-year, $8 million contract with the Vikings in June, will miss Monday night's game against the Buffalo Bills because of a strained calf that he suffered in practice this week. He missed a game in Week 2 while grieving the death of a family member, but in six appearances this season he has only 10 targets on 145 routes run. He has caught six of those passes for 54 yards, his lowest totals through eight weeks of a season since he was a part-time player with the 49ers in 2021. Much of that can be explained by the Vikings' intention to maximize targets to receivers Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison , as well as their use of tight end T.J. Hockenson as a safety valve in the middle of the field. The 49ers presumably had more robust plans for Jennings given their injuries this season at the position. "I'm not the coach, so I don't call the plays," Jennings said. "I'm a player, so I just play the game. I feel like anybody who watches football, who watches sports in general, kind of understands what comes with it." Jennings was particularly demonstrative on the sideline during a Week 5 victory at the New Orleans Saints , at one point pounding the turf on the sideline after he and quarterback Kyler Murray could not connect on a deep pass. The Vikings had signed veteran receiver Odell Beckham Jr . to their practice squad earlier that week, and they engaged the 49ers in trade talks not long after. The discussions advanced to the point where Jennings spoke with 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan. "He likes where he's at," Shanahan said earlier this week, "and I thought he made sense [with] what he said, and I agreed with him." Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell said he has spent "a lot of time talking to [Jennings] throughout the season" and added: "We really built up a strong relationship and out of the respect for the coach to player, that's one thing, but just the respect for our personal relationship that we have, just as we worked through that, I thought really both sides handled things the right way and ultimately I was super fired up that Jauan really enjoys it here, loves being a Minnesota Viking and that's kind of just where we left it." As of Saturday, the Vikings hadn't yet decided who would replace Jennings as the Vikings' No. 3 receiver on Monday night. Beckham is an option, O'Connell said, but he noted that Beckham has worked in practice mostly as a backup to the positions that Jefferson and Addison play, and only this week got reps at Jennings' "F" position. If Beckham isn't elevated for the game, the Vikings would use a combination of Tai Felton and Myles Price in the role. Other options to replace Jennings on the game-day roster are practice squad receivers Jeshaun Jones and Dillon Bell .

(Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins are heading into their Week 9 game against the Detroit Lions surprisingly healthy for a mid-season game. The Dolphins listed only three players on their final injury report on Friday, and all three were questionable at worst. Miami will likely have its entire roster available for the game. The Lions, meanwhile, ruled out five players, all starters. for the game. They also had three players listed as questionable. Kadyn Proctor returns Rookie guard Kadyn Proctor cleared concussion protocol after missing last week’s game against the New England Patriots. Proctor’s return to the lineup returns the Dolphins to their original starting lineup with left tackle Patrick Paul, left guard Proctor, center Aaron Brewer, right guard Jonah Savaiinaea, and right tackle Austin Jackson. On Friday, The Phinsider’s Marek Brave wrote, “ In [Proctor’s] absence , Miami’s offensive line struggled against a stout Patriots front — allowing 5 sacks and managing just 74 yards rushing on 20 attempts (just 3.7 yards per carry).“ Getting Proctor back into the lineup should assist the Dolphins as they face the ninth-ranked rush defense in the league on Sunday. Malik Willis downplays groin injury Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis, who was a full participant all week in practice, has been dealing with a groin injury for the last couple of week. He was asked this week if the injury led to a reluctance to run last week against the Patriots and he was pretty straight forward that they were not connected. “I think that’s just how the game played out. I’m not sure that had anything to do with it really,” he stated. Willis continued to be listed on the injury report this week with the injury, but was not given a game-day status, indicating he will be starting. Lions without several starters The Lions have not been as lucky with their injuries. Linebacker Jack Campbell, who sustained a serious neck injury early in last week’s game against the Minnesota Vikings, was obviously going to be ruled out of the game. Several other players were also given the “out” designation. Safety Kerby Joseph continues to work his way back from the physically unable to perform list with a knee injury. According to Pride of Detroit’s Erik Schlitt, the Lions plan on ramping up Joseph’s workload next week . He has a little over a week remaining on his practice window before the team has to move him to the 53-man roster or leave him on the PUP for the remainder of the year. Center Cade Mays has an ankle injury and the Lions have been preparing for him to be out this weekend. Juice Scruggs will start in his place. Cornerback D.J. Reed has a hip injury and has not been able to practice all week. Edge rusher DJ Wonnum has a concussion and is working his way through the protocols. Including Joseph, who will move into the starting lineup once he is activated off the PUP, all five players are starters for the Lions. Dolphins running backs questionable behind Ollie Gordon II The biggest injury concerns for the Dolphins heading into this weekend’s game may be at running back depth. While Ollie Gordon II, elevated to the starting role after De’Von Achane’s season-ending injury early this year, will see most snaps, both Jaylen Wright and Kaytron Allen are questionable for the game. While they will likely both be available, Miami’s depth may be fairly shallow if anything aggravates the quadriceps injuries nagging both players. Wright did not practice on Wednesday before being limited on both Thursday and Friday; Allen was limited for the first two days before being a full participant on Friday. Miami also listed edge rusher Malik Herring as questionable with a neck injury. He was limited in practice all week. stories.summary: The Cleveland Browns work is more difficult in Week 9 with the New Orleans Saints activating Jordyn Tyson, Kelvin Banks
stories.detailText: The big story heading into the Cleveland Browns matchup with the New Orleans Saints is the visiting team’s quarterback position. Shedeur Sanders will start , but Deshaun Watson has cleared concussion protocol and could be set to be the backup, after missing practice all week. On the other side, the home Saints are coming off their bye week, made a position coach change , and the final injury report provided hope that WR Jordyn Tyson and OT Kelvin Banks Jr. could return from injured reserve. Tyson, New Orleans’ first-round pick, has not played at all this season with a hamstring injury. Banks was the Saints’ first-round pick last season and started all 17 games for the team as a rookie in 2025, but went on injured reserve after two games this season. Saturday afternoon, New Orleans officially activated both Tyson and Banks off injured reserve, along with four other moves: Waived RB Kendre Miller Waived TE Treyton Welch Elevated K Charlie Smyth Elevated RB Zamir White Given Tyson’s injury history in college, it will be interesting how much playing time he is allowed in Week 9 against the Browns, while Banks is likely to take back over at left tackle.

stories.title: Maryland football survives late scare in 34-29 victory over Purdue
stories.summary: The Terps scored 27 second-half points in their come-from-behind victory.
stories.detailText: The University of Maryland Men’s Football Team was defeated by University of Illinois 20-17 at SECU Stadium on October 31th 2026. | Jessie Reider/Testudo Times With Purdue down to a fourth-and-10 from their own 5-yard line and 44 seconds remaining, it appeared Maryland football’s first Big Ten victory in 14 games was secured. But the Boilermakers weren’t done. “They don’t make it easy on me, man,” interim head coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim joked of his defense after the game. Purdue found a completion to extend its two-minute drill, and it kept moving downfield, arriving at Maryland’s 11-yard line with five seconds left. But an illegal substitution pushed the offense back, giving Maryland’s pass rush more time to deliver. And as quarterback Ryan Browne scrambled, Zion Elee spun him around, with Sidney Stewart delivering the leveling hit as time expired. The Terps held on to beat the Boilermakers, 34-29, for their first Big Ten win in 413 days. The matchup between teams that each have just two Big Ten wins over the last three seasons looked the part early, with the Terps and the Boilermakers combining for 69 first-quarter yards. Purdue got on the board first, kicking a field goal on a short drive after Bryce McFerson’s punt went just 27 yards. To start the second quarter, Maryland’s linebackers lost wide receiver Asaad Waseem on a crossing route, and he peeled away for a 37-yard reception that set up another field goal. Meanwhile, thanks to a Michael Hershey hands-in-the-face penalty that stalled out a promising drive, the Terps’ first 16 offensive plays netted them 40 yards. Maryland finally got past midfield with seven minutes to go in the first half, but that was because of an excellent kick return by Ricardo Cooper Jr. After that special teams spark, the Terps’ offense needed just three plays to reach the end zone. Malik Washington found Chris Durr Jr. in stride for a 31-yard gain before running in a 15-yard score off an option read. Fortunately for the Terps, that touchdown cut the lead to two points. Maryland’s defense bent to the tune of 156 second-quarter yards, but it refused to break, holding the Boilermakers to field goals on each of their first three red zone drives. After another Purdue field goal, Maryland’s two-minute drive was cut short by an incomprehensible interception — Washington’s pass hit Dorian Fleming’s ready hands and flew into the air for an easy pick. Purdue couldn’t capitalize, though. Elee sacked the quarterback on a crucial third down, pushing the Boilermakers back into a Hail Mary — where the freshman got home again to erase the turnover. Following the half, Maryland had four straight touchdowns, finding the scoring groove that had evaded it all season. The Terps’ offense earned its first second-half score, grinding over midfield before Na’eem Abdul-Rahim Gladding burst free from a crowded set for a 44-yard score. The second came from a piece of defensive fortune. Lavain Scruggs got into the backfield and stripped quarterback Ryan Browne, with the Terps recovering on the two-yard line. But on three tries, the run game struck out. Washington, rushed back onto the field with an injured knee, took matters into his own hands. Receiving the fourth-down snap under center, Washington rose up, cresting over his offensive line to reach the ball into the end zone. Purdue got a touchdown back, courtesy of some big plays that moved the chains. But DeJuan Williams responded with an even bigger play, running 75 yards untouched into the end zone on the offense’s first snap back on the field. Maryland’s defense again held strong in the red zone, forcing the Boilermakers to kick a field goal after having first-and-goal three yards out. Purdue almost immediately paid for coming short. Cooper scampered away on another kickoff, this time reaching the end zone. However, a block in the back by Jayden Kitchens nullified the score, bringing Maryland back to the 12-yard line. Durr, who had cooled off through October after a fiery start to the season, had a piece of individual brilliance to give the Terps just enough cushion. Catching a screen deep in the left flat, the Wyoming transfer sliced through the entire defense, climbing the ladder to the right sideline and sprinting to the end zone for an 87-yard score. Purdue cut the score with a 13-play, 75-yard drive, and it fended off the Terps’ offense around midfield to earn one more possession. Ultimately, though, Maryland’s red zone defense came out on top. Three things to know 1. Backfield pressure wins the game. The Terps finished Saturday’s game with seven sacks, their most since 2020, and a season-high 13 total tackles for loss. Alongside Elee and his 2.5 sacks, Nahsir Taylor, Trey Reddick and CJ Smith each had multiple tackles for loss. 2. Punting battle lost. McFerson has struggled in 2026 — the preseason Ray Guy watch list punter’s 42.21 yard per punt average entering Saturday was second-worst in the Big Ten. With Maryland needing to scrap for field position against the Boilermakers, McFerson’s first two punts went for a combined 62 yards. But the senior finally had a short punt go his way, pinning Purdue at the 5-yard line for its final drive. 3. Terps lost their tempers. Five plays into the game, embattled cornerback Dontay Joyner was ejected. Referees determined he threw a punch; three plays earlier, he had also thrown a slap at an opponent. Joyner’s was one of nine Maryland penalties on the afternoon. Emotions remained at a simmer throughout. Messiah Delhomme, DD Holmes and Elee scuffled along the Boilermakers’ sideline in the third quarter; only Elee escaped without a personal foul, but none were ejected. The trio continued to make plays to seal the game.

stories.title: 49ers Mailbag: Should the team get more defensive line help? What’s up with the return/kicking game?
stories.summary: You’ve got questions? I will make you ask more questions
stories.detailText: SANTA CLARA, CA - DECEMBER 23: DeForest Buckner #99 of the San Francisco 49ers in action during the game against the Chicago Bears at Levi Stadium on December 23, 2018 in Santa Clara, CA. The Bears defeated the 49ers 14-9. (Photo by Rob Leiter/Getty Images) | Getty Images What? You mean you guys like these things? We haven’t done too many mailbags this year, but maybe I can change that. Because of the timing, I wasn’t able to get to every question asked in my call for submissions, but keep an eye out for the next one. I post over in the Niners Nation Feed when I’m going to do a mailbag, and I’ll be sure to not do it on a Thursday this time. By the way, if you haven’t gone to The Feed yet, what’s stopping you? Not only am I there, but Fooch posts there a lot, too. Come hang out with the Niners Nation alum! Now, as for this week, this is going up Saturday afternoon, and the San Francisco 49ers are preparing for the Las Vegas Raiders. This seems like another tricky game for the team. Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins always seems to play well against the 49ers, like some long-standing grudge against Kyle Shanahan when the former was going to come in a few years before the latter traded for Jimmy Garoppolo. I think the 49ers can pull off the victory—based on the Raiders starting to remember they are the Raiders—but they can’t make the same mistakes they did against the Atlanta Falcons. Ok, onto your questions: If a Pontiac and a Buick both leave Chicago at the same time………. —NYners They both will have engine failure two miles outside of city limits. And keeping with the STs theme — why do they still have faith in Cowing returning punts? I’m terrified he’s gonna drop it, even on a fair catch. If the former Ram who’s on the practice squad isn’t any better, why do we even have him on the team? —TheGoldenRatio Probably because they don’t want to pull from the very limited pool of wide receivers they already have and risk someone else getting beat up on the return game. I have to think that as the wide receivers come back, the 49ers move to…well…moving on from Cowing. At least at returner. They have Brandin Cooks on the roster, and while he’s not as fast as he was a decade ago, he’s still got some wheels and has been a returner in the past. De’Zhaun Stribling could also be a good option, but for reasons I just outlined, they may want him fresh for the offense and not on return duty because they aren’t going to be able to rely on Mike Evans for every play. I can’t fathom a situation where Cowing is the punt returner in January based on what we’ve seen. This isn’t even about his ball security issues; it’s about his decision-making. I’m of the mind that our D line is pretty awesome with Defo and Bosa on the field. My only reservation is injuries, especially Bosa. Do we really need to make a splash with an extra Edge? White, Williams and Height seems like a good rotation across from Bosa. — 80849er It could help, but I also think the 49ers need to hold onto some draft picks and salary cap space. Whoever they bring in, they have to make room for by releasing someone else, allocating what is the thinnest of margins in cap space, and sacrificing development of their younger talent. Not to mention draft picks. It’s not the greatest answer, but when they bring in a Khalil Mack or some sort, that’s going to take snaps away from a younger player who needs that experience and fewer picks to get more ammo in case that younger player doesn’t work out. I want to win now, just like all of you do, but not at the cost of development to stay competitive. I am not a fan of the Los Angeles’ Rams way of just “buying” a Super Bowl for one year. Some players you know won’t click; others need to be on the field and mess up, even in a championship season. The DeForest Buckner trade was great because while it removed snaps, it didn’t do so much that it tossed the depth chart to the bench. Adding more could make things cramped. It also helped with the culture since Buckner has been there before and can be a good mentor Speaking of which, that has already been paying dividends for young talent. Romello Height is getting up a bit earlier now , for one thing. The others have a lot to learn from Buckner as a player, and it’s already rubbing off. Has something changed in Piñeiro’s mechanics, or with the snap and hold timing? Is he more accurate from one hash mark or another? How does he compare to the league average percentage of missed extra points? Why hasn’t the team brought in another kicker for a tryout? Why haven’t they brought someone else in? Probably because Piñeiro just signed an extension with $10 million in guaranteed money. Kyle Shanahan did seem a bit miffed after the Atlanta game, but shortly after that, John Lynch affirmed the 49ers were sticking with Piñeiro. If you were wanting kicker tryouts—those aren’t happening. Have we hit David Akers or even Jake Moody levels of kicking? It’s a rough patch, but I give him a couple more games. If he misses more XPs in the next two games, regardless of whether it’s a victory or loss, the 49ers have to do something. It’s just like if their punt returner had bad ball security and they did nothing… Brandon Aiyuk owes the 49ers $13 million. If you’d signed that contract, what would you have spent the $13 million on? —Fooch I’d go to Vegas and make max bets on Casino War while getting bottle service. I’d set aside half for an executive suite at Levi’s Stadium for one game. I’d also buy a sealed copy of Panzer Dragoon Saga for the Sega Saturn. If there’s money leftover I’ll also buy a gold cart of Nintendo World Championships .

stories.title: Saints activate WR Jordyn Tyson, LT Kelvin Banks, cut RB Kendre Miller
stories.summary: Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. have been activated from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game against the Browns.
stories.detailText: New Orleans Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. have been activated from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns . Tyson, the eighth overall pick in the 2026 draft, is set to make his NFL debut after injuring his hamstring in August. He returned to practice for the first time since injuring his right hamstring in a joint practice against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Aug. 13. He has been listed as questionable on the injury report along with Banks, who also returned to practice following surgery on his ankle. Tyson was expected to be out at least two months after the hamstring injury, which occurred after he landed awkwardly after catching a pass. Both Tyson and the Saints said the injury was not related to his previous hamstring issues from college; he missed three games for Arizona State last year. He also tore his ACL, MCL and PCL in his left knee when he was at Colorado in 2022, fractured his collarbone in 2024 and sprained his ankle that caused him to miss spring practices in 2025. Tyson said he feels like the extended time to get himself right has been "a blessing." "Kind of got a slow start to the NFL, so I got to kind of take my time and kind of really adjust to it," he said. The Saints released running back Kendre Miller as a corresponding move. Miller, a 2023 third-round pick out of TCU , led the Saints' struggling run game with 159 yards this season. The Saints released him after claiming running back Audric Estime off waivers from the Cleveland Browns . Estime was with the team last year and in camp but was waived with an injury settlement. The Saints rushed for only 18 yards in their last game before the bye week, a 16-10 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris.

Pop Douglas, Efton Chism, and Kyle Williams join Hollins as the available receivers on the 53-man roster for New England.

stories.title: Lions place Jack Campbell on IR, sign PS CB to active roster
stories.summary: Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell has been placed on IR after a serious neck injury.
stories.detailText: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 1: Jack Campbell #46 of the Detroit Lions runs onto the field prior to the game against the Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field on November 1, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions made several roster moves on Saturday morning, but there was none more notable than placing All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell on injured reserve. The Lions’ defense captain suffered a serious neck injury during last week’s game against the Minnesota Vikings. Campbell was transferred to a nearby hospital and offered the following update on his condition Wednesday via an official statement . “I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body,” Campbell said. “I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better.” Since then, Lions coach Dan Campbell has said Campbell continues to improve. At this point, it’s unclear what Campbell’s injury means for the rest of the season or his career, but his placement on injured reserve guarantees he must miss the next four games. The first game he’d be eligible to return is Week 13 vs. the Atlanta Falcons on December 6. In Campbell’s place, the Lions are expected to start Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez, and Trevor Nowaske at linebacker vs. the Miami Dolphins. Detroit will also have Joe Bachie, K.J. Britt, and Amen Ogbongbemiga available among their reserves. To take Campbell’s spot on the 53-man roster, the Lions signed cornerback Nick Whiteside from the practice squad. Whiteside made a strong impression during training camp, even earning some reps with the first-team defense during early practices. Now, with top cornerback D.J. Reed out this week with a hip injury , Whiteside has an opportunity to be part of the Lions’ cornerback rotation, which will likely include Roger McCreary, Ennis Rakestraw, Rock Ya-Sin, and Khalil Dorsey. In addition to those two moves, the Lions also elevated defensive end Anthony Lucas and running back Jabari Small from the practice squad. We have more information on those moves in a separate news article .

stories.summary: Cleveland GM Andrew Berry continues to look for help along the bottom of the roster and practice squad.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns have dealt with their share of injuries this season, especially at certain positions. Running backs Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson have both missed time, as have defensive tackles Mason Graham, Mike Hall Jr., and Maliek Collins, who is out for Sunday’s game against New Orleans with an elbow injury . As general manager Andrew Berry shuffles the game-day roster, he also looks for players to fill out the bottom of the roster and practice squad. And on Friday, the Browns hosted running backs Ulysses Bentley IV and Elijah Tau-Tolliver, and defensive backs Austin Brown, Darren Hall, and Jerrick Reed. #Browns worked out Ulysses Bentley, Austin Brown, Darren Hall, Jerrick Reed, Elijah Tau-Tolliver — Aaron Wilson (@AaronWilson_NFL) November 7, 2026 The 5-foot-10 and 200-pound Bentley originally signed with the Indianapolis Colts in 2025 as an undrafted free agent out of Ole Miss. stories.title: Hall of Famer Jack Ham hospitalized after medical emergency
stories.summary: Hall of Fame linebacker and Penn State radio analyst Jack Ham experienced a medical emergency Saturday in Seattle and is being treated at a hospital.
stories.detailText: Hall of Fame linebacker and Penn State radio analyst Jack Ham experienced a medical emergency Saturday in Seattle and is being treated at a hospital. In a statement, Penn State said Ham, 77, was transported to University of Washington Medical Center. The school did not provide any further details about his condition. Ham has been the radio analyst for his alma mater since 2000. Penn State is in Seattle to face Washington on Saturday night. Ham was a six-time All-Pro selection with the Pittsburgh Steelers , where he won four Super Bowl championships and made eight total Pro Bowl appearance. He earned All-America honors at Penn State in 1970. He entered the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1988 and the College Football Hall of Fame two years later. The Johnstown, Pennsylvania, native was named to the NFL's 1970s All-Decade Team and all-time teams for both the NFL and Steelers, who have Ham in their hall of honor.
