stories.title: A Bears win on Sunday could catapult Caleb Williams back into the MVP race
stories.summary: What would another primetime win mean for the Chicago Bears and Caleb Williams?
stories.detailText: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 2: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears reacts after the game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on November 2, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Before the 2026 season started, Caleb Williams was seen as a dark-horse MVP candidate. He was coming off an exciting first year with Ben Johnson, with a highlight reel a mile long. He was the Madden cover athlete, and as the offseason progressed, the buzz around Caleb and the Chicago Bears kept building. After they dropped a 50-burger in Week 1, the NFL shifted the hype train into high gear, and the Bears were the lead story on every NFL show. But then Week 2 and Brian Flores’ Minnesota Vikings defense came to town, and coupled with a steady downpour, Chicago’s offense never got on track. Then a fourth-quarter hamstring injury as the Bears were driving inside the Minnesota 1o yard line would sideline Williams for the next three games, seemingly ending his Most Valuable Player chances. The Bears went 2-1 in his absence, but since his return, Williams and the Bears haven’t trailed in any of their three games, and he’s completing 73.8% of his passes for 860 yards, 4 touchdowns, no turnovers, and a passer rating of 111.3. The last two weeks, he diced up the defenses of the last two Super Bowl teams, and his MVP odds have shot back up according to our partners at FanDuel Sportsbook . Right now, he’s at +800 to win MVP, trailing only the Buffalo Bills’ Josh Allen (+175), the Cincinnati Bengals’ Joe Burrow (+450), the San Fransocso 49ers’ Brock Purdy (+550 ), and the Jacksonville Jaguars’ Trevor Lawrence (+600). Earlier this week, we outlined how difficult it has been historically for a player to win the Most Valuable Player award after missing time during the season, but there is a precedent for him to do it, and another big game on Sunday Night Football could get him back in the conversation.

stories.title: Colts elevate two defensive backs to the active roster and rule out starting safety
stories.summary: The Colts are bolstering their DB depth ahead of Sunday because of recent injuries.
stories.detailText: BALTIMORE, MD - AUGUST 7: Johnathan Edwards #35 of the Indianapolis Colts in coverage during an NFL Preseason 2025 game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on August 7, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Saturday, the Indianapolis Colts announced that the team has elevated cornerback Johnathan Edwards and safety Trey Washington from their practice squad ahead of Sunday’s home game against the Dallas Cowboys: We have elevated CB Johnathan Edwards and S Trey Washington to the active roster from the practice squad for #DALvsIND . — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) November 7, 2026 The team also announced that starting rookie safety AJ Haulcy (ankle) has been downgraded to out , with fellow defensive starters: linebacker Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee) and slot cornerback Justin Walley (knee) already ruled out for Sunday’s game. Given the injuries to both Haulcy and Walley, it makes sense as to why both Edwards at cornerback and Washington at safety were added to the Colts’ 53-man active roster. Neither defensive back will fill in as a replacement starter, as that should fall upon Kapena Gushiken and Hunter Wohler respectively. That being said, both backup defensive backs should provide additional depth and special teams work.

stories.title: Who are the Steelers taking in expert mock drafts?
stories.summary: The Steelers don’t play this week, making it a great opportunity to look ahead to the 2027 NFL Draft.
stories.detailText: Photo by Soobum Im/Getty Images | Getty Images Is it too early to talk about the NFL Draft? There are always those that say “never,” but for many, draft season doesn’t start until the Steelers have played their last snap of the season in the early months of the new year. However, Pittsburgh’s bye week always presents a good time to take a step back from the storylines of the current season and evaluate the bigger picture. Just how good are the Steelers ? What are their biggest roster needs? And who are some early targets in the upcoming 2027 draft? With no game this weekend to distract from, here are six recent national NFL mock drafts and the Steelers’ projected first-round selection in each. You can click on each pick’s heading to read the full draft and see who was available when Pittsburgh was “on the clock.” Let’s dive in: Pick 27: Dante Moore, QB, Oregon Fox Sports’ Rob Rang: Given the investment made in Drew Allar last spring, I don’t believe the Steelers are planning to draft a quarterback in the first round of the 2027 draft. However, should an abbreviated 2026 season push Dante Moore — the most talented passer in this class — far enough down the board, it would make sense for Pittsburgh to adjust its plan. Pick 27: Ellis Robinson IV, CB, Georgia A to Z Sports’ Kyle Crabbs and Rob Gregson: While Jamel Dean, Asante Samuel Jr. and Daylen Everette have done a nice job this season, Ellis Robinson IV would transform that secondary. He’s one of the most complete corners in this class, and he plays with a physicality and tenacity that scream Pittsburgh. Pick 28: Trinidad Chambliss, QB, Ole Miss CBS Sports’ Ryan Wilson: The Steelers need a QB. This is not up for debate. But do they roll with ’26 third-rounder Drew Allar? Would, say, 6-foot-4 Austin Simmons make more sense here? Or does Mike McCarthy roll the dice on Chambliss, who is not 6-foot but has played a lot of high-level SEC football and is a proven winner? Pick 22: Kelley Jones, CB, Mississippi State USA Today’s Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Grappling with the likes of Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins is never fun for opponents. That’s the Steelers’ reality for the foreseeable future, however, and sending off Joey Porter Jr. only complicates that task. At 6-4 and 205 pounds, Jones combines the size to pester both well-built receivers and the speed to stick close by each one. Pick 28: Jadan Baugh, RB, Florida Sports Illustrated’s Justin Melo: The Pittsburgh Steelers will probably transition to Will Howard or Drew Allar at quarterback next season. They should explore their potential post-Aaron Rodgers before spending another pick at quarterback. They could help their young starter by adding a workhorse running back like Florida’s Jadan Baugh. Pick 28: Tae Johnson, S, Notre Dame NFL Stock Exchange’s Connor Rogers: “I think (the Steelers) offensive line has a lot of young talent, and it feels like they’re probably pretty excited about Drew Allar after Aaron Rodgers — I’m not really thinking quarterback here yet. … I literally looked up DK (Metcalf’s) contract wondering about (drafting Texas’ Cam Coleman), but it’s not pretty, so it’s not happening here. … But when you watch Tae Johnson’s 2025 tape, it’s game-changing safety-level stuff. If he’s healthy and comes back this year and returns to the form he had last year, this is well worth this selection. The Steelers are currently on track to pick in the late-20s of the first round. Currently, the team has nine picks in 2027: one each in Rounds 1 and 2, two in Round 3, none in Round 4, one in Round 5 and two each in Rounds 6 and 7. The Steelers are not projected to earn any compensatory picks in 2027 according to Over the Cap. Which of the above players caught your eye the most? Which position do you think the Steelers will target in the first round? Want to make any way-too-early predictions yourself? Join the BTSC community and let us know in the comments.

stories.title: Falcons vs. Bengals series history: Win-loss record, matchup results
stories.summary: The Falcons look to end a losing streak.
stories.detailText: 24 Nov 1996: Running back Jamal Anderson #32 of the Atlanta Falcons carries the football during the Falcons 41-31 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals at Riverfront Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio. Mandatory Credit: Jed Jacobsohn /Allsport | Getty Images The Falcons head back into play against the AFC this week, and they do so across the pond in the second ever NFL game to be played in the Spanish capital of Madrid, at the esteemed Estadio de Santiago Bernebéu. Their opponent in that game will be the Cincinnati Bengals, who have won two games out of every three against the Birds, owning a very aesthetically pleasing 10-5 all time record against Atlanta. The majority of that damage came before the turn of the millennia, with the Bengals winning seven out of 10 matchups against the overmatched Falcons through the 1996 season, with games between these teams happening on averaged every three years in that time period. The Birds pulled back a little bit with three consecutive victories — in 2002, 2006 and 2010 — to pull the series close to even. That was quickly followed with three straight Bengals victories which brings us to where we are today, with two of those coming in the Matt Ryan era, which was also the most successful one in Falcons history. The Bengals caught Atlanta in a down year of that era twice in a row, in 2014 and 2018. When these teams met last The Falcons had some confidence about them in year 2 of the Arthur Smith regime, having just pulled back to .500 at 3-3, with a victory against the 49ers after some questionable reffing cost them against Tampa the week before. The Bengals sported the same record, but they proved from the start that they were on another level. It took exactly two minutes for second year man Joe Burrow to hit Tyler Boyd on a 60-yard touchdown to open the scoring. Then after a Falcon punt, the Bengals punched the ball in again following a longer drive. Then an Atlanta three and out was followed with a Burrow to rookie Ja’Marr Chase touchdown on the first play of the second quarter, before the two connected in the end zone again on the back end of the same quarter. By halftime the game was effectively over as the Falcon offense spent the second half completely one dimensional and getting terrorized by the Bengal defense, with Burrow putting the finishing touches on with a rushing score to complete his magnificent day. Up 35-17, one of the most impressive feats by the Bengal offense was getting the ball back via punt at their own 3-yard-line (why the Falcons punted it near midfield down three scores in the fourth quarter I don’t know) with 8:44 left in the game and choking away that entire clock (and all three Atlanta timeouts) with a 17-play drive which went 95 yards and ended in a kneel down.

stories.title: AP readers’ 2026 Midseason Hot Seat watch for NFL coaches
stories.summary: Which NFL Head Coach will be the first to go this season?
stories.detailText: (Robert Gauthier/Los Angeles Times via Getty Images) A month ago , we asked our readers to give us a list of head coaches who should be on the hot seat. At the time, you guys told us that the person who should have the hottest tushy was the head coach of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , Todd Bowles. In second place was Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur, and rounding out the list was Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh. The NFL is a wild place, and a lot can happen in a month. Since our last edition of this series, two of the three coaches who were previously predicted to be on their way out have found a way to right their ship enough for the time being to at least work their way off this list. But one coach has not disappointed and has lived up to our expectations of sub-par performance. Heck, some might even say his team has exceeded expectations of just how truly awful they can be. When it comes to sucking, this guy is the gold standard. Here is what you said. 1. Jim Harbaugh – Los Angeles Chargers Previous Ranking: 3 Heat Rating: Like every fart he has ever had in his entire life is coming out all at once Harbaugh (seen in the image above showing one of his players what his pet turtle looks like when it’s trying to eat lettuce) has been hard at work moving up the charts. Jumping from third place to first, Captain Khaki Pants has continued to be haunted by the angry spirits of the San Diego faithful, who are still angry that the team left their lovely city in favor of being Los Angeles’ unwanted stepchild. The Chargers have lost their last two games by double digits, with their most recent loss coming to their big brothers, the Los Angeles Rams , who held Harbaugh’s team to just nine points. Quarterback Justin Herbert continues to have the worst season of his career — with a season QBR of just 32.5, he’s currently sporting an uninspiring 5/10 interception-to-touchdown ratio. The Chargers are by far the worst team in the league. The only question is: can Harbaugh buy himself one more year by throwing his coordinators under the bus to save his own skin? What if every fart you have ever done come out once? We did the math. pic.twitter.com/A8cA0UESDQ — Way Of Discipline (@wayofdiscipline) November 6, 2026 Here is what you had to say: “Andy Reid /s But seriously, Dave Toub should be. Not quite sure why he’s still a Chief. head coaches? Dan Quinn, Jim Harbaugh, Dave Canales” – Phoenix_Chief 2. Nick Sirianni- Philadelphia Eagles Previous Ranking: N/A Heat Rating: On the toilet after appearing on the YouTube series “Hot Ones.” Sirianni (seen here looking down at his shoes and trying to remember if he put them on the right feet) is the only coach on this list to have won a Super Bowl. At first glance, it might seem a little unfair to have Sirianni on this list, especially when you consider he lost his starting quarterback for the season, and his best offensive lineman (Lane Johnson) decided to retire mid-year. But the Eagles have dropped six in a row, and this isn’t the first time a Sirianni-coached team has folded under pressure. In 2021, the Eagles were 10-1, heading into Week 13, and proceeded to go 1-5 the rest of the way to close out the season, squeaking into the playoffs as a wildcard, where they promptly got bounced by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 32-9. Also, it’s a little hard to feel bad for anyone in the Eagles organization this season, when the Eagles’ starting quarterback, Jalen Hurts, had a serious medical emergency due to his diagnosis of blood clots in his lungs being mishandled by the team. bill murray's reaction to every wing on hot ones 💪 (and pete davidson's reaction to the last dab 🫠 ) pic.twitter.com/x5ezxTUgZC — First We Feast (@firstwefeast) March 6, 2025 Here is what you had to say: “Siriani has got to be sitting on a cast iron skillet at the very least” – Andyreidsmustache_ 3. Dan Quinn- Washington Commanders Previous Ranking: N/A Heat Rating: Sitting too close to the campfire so that the soles on your shoes start to melt Since making a surprise appearance in the NFC Championship game in 2024, Dan Quinn (pictured above thinking he just had to toot, but realizing a little bit more came out) and the Commanders have gone 7-16 combined. That’s a .304 winning percentage over the last two seasons. Some may give Quinn a pass because his franchise quarterback, Jayden Daniels, has been a regular on the injured list. But let’s be real: the NFL is a results-driven industry, and fair or not, the output just hasn’t been there. Quinn made his name in the NFL as a defensive coordinator with the Seattle Seahawks , so it’s a tough look when the only team you’ve held to under 20 points on the season is the aforementioned Eagles. Especially when three teams have dropped 30+ points on you so far this year. Here is what you had to say: “Harbaugh, Schottenheimer, Siriani, and quinn all will be gone” – chiefhawk Guys who should be monitoring the temperature of their cheeks: Shane Steichen ( Indianapolis Colts ), Dave Canales ( Carolina Panthers ), and Brian Schottenheimer ( Dallas Cowboys )

stories.title: Cowboys two keys to beating Colts and keeping playoffs hopes alive
stories.summary: The Cowboys need a win in the worst way
stories.detailText: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys have very possibly not yet defined what “rock bottom” could look like on this 2026 season, but any version of sinking lower than they are right now would involve a second straight loss to a losing team this upcoming Sunday afternoon. The Cowboys are at the Colts, who have not won in over a month. Many things about this matchup make it feel like it’s an opportunity sitting on a tee for Brian Schottenheimer’s team to get back in the win column, and just maybe make the run-in to Thanksgiving interesting. It’s time for our weekly look at how the Cowboys can keep alternating wins and losses by bouncing back in week nine, or how they could send this season farther down the drain with another bad loss. The Dallas Cowboys will beat the Indianapolis Colts if… …they don’t turn the ball over. Old friend Daniel Jones at QB for the Colts is the next opponent for the Cowboys to put pressure on, both with their defense (more on that later) and ideally the offense too, by possessing the ball and scoring touchdowns. Jones is 1-8 in his career against the Cowboys, from his past time with the Giants, with four touchdowns and six interceptions in these nine games. At all three levels of the Colts defense right now, they have problems. Up front, they just traded away DeForest Buckner. At linebacker, Akeem Davis-Gaither will be out on Sunday, with the team already starting rookie C.J. Allen at one of the linebacker positions. In the secondary, former Cowboy Charvarius Ward and Sauce Gardner have not played up to potential and are prone to being beat over the top, and committing costly penalties. Nickel defender Justin Walley is also ruled out against the Cowboys. The Colts also have the worst turnover differential in the league this season, and have been minus three in two of their last three games, both divisional losses. They do not have a game with a positive margin, and their only neutral game was still a 34-22 loss to Mike McCarthy’s Steelers. With CeeDee Lamb telling the media this week he views the Cowboys offense as beating themselves more than anything, there should be no excuse to not execute the basics against the Colts. Not every drive has to end in points, but not having the focus to stay on the field in short-yardage situations, not getting backed up by unforced penalties, and not finding ways to get the ball to Lamb and George Pickens in space to lean on the Colts all afternoon with this highly-paid offense would be an abject failure. The Colts defense has not taken the ball away once throughout their active four-game losing streak. If the Cowboys don’t turn the ball over and give the Colts extra life and short fields to keep the game close, the talent differential in this matchup should reveal itself and allow the Cowboys to get out of Indy with a win. The Dallas Cowboys will lose to the Indianapolis Colts if… …they don’t get to Daniel Jones. Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor might be the obvious choice as the potential game-wrecker against the Cowboys defense in this matchup, especially considering the Colts main objective may actually be getting Taylor’s trade value up with a big game against a Dallas defense torched by Tyler Allgeier last week. Allgeier was certainly a big factor in how the Cardinals made their comeback in Arlington last Sunday, but when the game clearly came down to Gardner Minshew needing to make a throw, he did so as well for the real backbreaking plays against Christian Parker’s defense. The Cowboys also sacked Jacoby Brissett four times last week, but only got to Minshew once with Quinnen Williams doing so in overtime. Daniel Jones was sacked three times last Sunday against the Jags. He was sacked four times against a Vikings defense that blitzed him at a relentless rate that literally broke records for how often a defense could blitz. The week before that, he was sacked six times against the Titans. The Steelers defense only got to Jones once, but still swung the game in their favor by forcing Jones to drop back 44 times compared to 24 total rushing attempts for the Colts in week five. In Jones’ last four starts against the Cowboys, all losses, he’s been sacked 16 times. Narrow this down to the last two games, and the Cowboys have won by a combined score of 60-15 with eight sacks, and also three interceptions. Whether it’s with the blitz or trusting Williams, Rashan Gary, and Donovan Ezeiruaku up front, Parker’s defense needs to make pressure the priority against this Colts offense. The coverage is not good enough to hold up for long enough periods of time to be trusted more than the Cowboys should trust their ability to get to Jones before he can even throw the ball, and the same goes for run defense. Sacks to get the Colts behind the chains is what this defense should be after more than anything. If the Cowboys continue to struggle finishing around the quarterback and allow Jones to extend plays, it will equally keep Jonathan Taylor as a threat in this game, and could make for a longer than anticipated afternoon trying to beat a team that’s already waved a white flag.

stories.title: Cowboys place OLB Malachi Lawrence on IR, activate OLB Marist Liufau from IR
stories.summary: The Cowboys placed outside linebacker Malachi Lawrence on injured reserve, the team announced Saturday.
stories.detailText: The Cowboys placed outside linebacker Malachi Lawrence on injured reserve, the team announced Saturday. Lawrence injured his ankle in Sunday's loss to the Cardinals, and coach Brian Schottenheimer had announced the rookie would miss multiple weeks. Lawrence will miss at least four games on IR. The first-round pick has 13 tackles, a sack and three quarterback hits, while playing 41 percent of the defensive snaps. In a corresponding move, the Cowboys activated outside linebacker Marist Liufau from injured reserve. Liufau broke his forearm in the preseason finale. He returned to practice Oct. 22. Cowboys defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard, who is in his 21-day return-to-practice window, will remain on injured reserve. He has a calf injury but had full practices all week. The Cowboys also announced they elevated wide receiver Jordan Hudson and tight end James Mitchell from the practice squad. Tight ends Jake Ferguson and Luke Schoonmaker are questionable to play, and at wide receiver, KaVontae Turpin is out and George Pickens is questionable.

stories.title: Commanders activate DT Johnny Newton from injured reserve
stories.summary: The Commanders are activating defensive tackle Johnny Newton from injured reserve, Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports.
stories.detailText: The Commanders are activating defensive tackle Johnny Newton from injured reserve, Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports. Newton has spent the season on IR after tearing a pectoral muscle in the preseason. He returned to practice Oct. 28, opening his 21-day window. Newton was limited in the Week 7 practices. He returned to full participation this week and had a questionable designation. He missed only one game over his first two seasons and totaled 82 tackles, seven sacks, two forced fumbles and two passes defensed.

stories.summary: Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow had seven touchdown passes in his team's first four games of the season.
stories.detailText: Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow had seven touchdown passes in his team's first four games of the season. In the last three, he has had 13. With four against the Dolphins, four against the Ravens, and five against the Titans, Burrow has the chance to become only the third quarterback in NFL history to throw four or more touchdown passes in four straight games. Via NBC Sports research, the two others were Colts quarterback Peyton Manning in 2004 and Dolphins quarterback Dan Marino in 1984. Both won the league MVP award in their seasons of four straight four-or-more touchdown games. Burrow's odds of winning the MVP for 2026 are currently at +475, behind only Josh Allen and Brock Purdy. Burrow currently leads the league with 20 touchdown passes. And the Bengals, after starting 2-2, are now 5-2. They face the 3-5 Falcons on Sunday morning in Madrid at 9:30 a.m. ET on Sunday.

stories.summary: Browns QB Deshaun Watson is out of the concussion protocol, but he is questionable. Shedeur Sanders will get the start against the Saints.
stories.detailText: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson has cleared concussion protocol, but he remains questionable for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints . Browns coach Todd Monken said Friday that Shedeur Sanders will get the start. It's unclear if Watson will serve as the backup or if that responsibility will fall to Dillon Gabriel or Taylen Green . Sanders has attempted just three passes this season in spot appearances during two games. He took all the starting reps in practice this week after Watson self-reported concussion symptoms Tuesday morning and was placed in the protocol. As a rookie last season, Sanders made seven starts, completing 56.6% of his passes for 1,400 yards with seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. He went 3-4 in those starts. Cleveland (5-3) faces the Saints this week and then hosts the Houston Texans in Week 10 before entering their bye. Information from ESPN's Daniel Oyefusi was used in this report.

stories.title: 5 Qs, 5 As: Washington fans ‘hate’ the name Commanders
stories.summary: What Commanders writers have to say about the team — and their name
stories.detailText: The Washington football team (not to be confused with the Washington Football Team) is on their fifth season of being named the Commanders. And it sounds as though fans of the team are no bigger fans of “Commanders” today than they were in 2022. In fact, the longer they go into the name change, the more they might want to change it again. It’s hard for me to imagine or accept that there is a team in the NFL named the “Commanders”, which still feels like a made-up name for a fictional pro football league in a Keanu Reeves or Kevin Costner movie. Even so, this is the name that they’re stuck with today, and it is the team that the Los Angeles Rams will face on Sunday in a critical moment for both franchises: If the Rams lose, all hell could break loose before the trade deadline Tuesday. If the Commanders lose, head coach Dan Quinn may not be associated with the “football team” by Monday . Washington is 2-4-1 and seeking their second win in a row since the return of quarterback Jayden Daniels. To get to know them — and their Football Team Fans — better, I sent five questions to Andrew Y at Hogs Haven. He sent me back five answers. Go…Team. Q: The Commanders don’t have a player in the top-30 for rushing yards or the top-60 for receiving yards. I feel like that would be very disappointing for fans, to not have one skill player so far this season who you can at least look forward to watching, win or lose. But those are stats, not necessarily reality. Who is the one healthy skill player on the team who Washington fans can look forward to watching each week? A: I think the player most Commanders fans would point to is rookie WR and 3rd-round pick Antonio Williams. He’s shown tremendous route-running nuance and short-area quickness to get open in the middle field and has been a consistent target getter, with 23 catches for 259 yards so far this season. Those simple stats don’t rely do credit to his ability though, as he’s generated a 96.7 passer rating when targeted and is PFF’s second-highest graded rookie receiver. Dan Quinn made clear that with the loss of Terry McLaurin, he expects Antonio Williams’ role to increase the most and indeed Williams led all receivers in snaps and routes last week against the Eagles. Q: Five years in, how is the name “Commanders” sitting with fans? Do you ever long for the days of Football Team again? A: Honestly, I think most fans hate the name Commanders. It’s the last stinky gift given to us by former owner Dan Snyder that the new leadership hasn’t been able to reverse. The names that seemed most popular with fans (and with me) were Red Wolves (a nod to the old name, but with a cool animal attached) or Warthogs (which has alliteration with Washington and could be shortened to ‘Hogs to reference the famous Hogs offensive line of the glory days). There is a contingent of fans that actually liked the name Washington Football Team and many would probably still take it over Commanders, but I always suspected it was more driven by nostalgia for the old name and a feeling that if we can’t have that name, then no name is better. Washington Football Team feels to me more like having no name and certainly doesn’t lend itself to new branding. I’d rather have a new team name and branding, it just needs to be a good name and good branding. Q: It’s the end of 2026 and the beginning of 2027. No changes have been made yet. Dan Quinn is the head coach, Adam Peters is the GM, the roster is intact. If you can make one change to the Commanders team/organization to set them on the right path, what do you do? A: Unless the rest of the season plays out very differently than it has up until now, I would fire Dan Quinn and let Adam Peters lead a search to choose the next head coach. I think Adam Peters has actually done a pretty good job of rebuilding the roster and giving the team enough depth to withstand an avalanche of injuries this year. However, they often look poorly coached, with the most yards erased by penalty in the NFL, slow playcalls and players taking too much time to get into position, and regular mistakes in situational awareness and game management that lose games. However, one other change needs to be made. The biggest reason the team was able to go on that 2024 playoff run and has been unable to repeat is that our 2024 season was one of our healthiest ever, with few major injuries to core players in the regular season. That’s a major outlier, as Washington has had the most Adjusted Games Lost (AGL) due to injury in the NFL since 2009 (!) and only the Giants have been in the same tier of AGL. This year is no different, with four of the team’s highest-paid players already done for the season. To be one of the NFL’s most-injured teams over that span of time is significant and unusual in that it covers multiple front office staffs, coaching staffs, and even medical staffs. The one constant in that time has been the strength and conditioning staff, led by Chad Englehart. Englehart started as an assistant strength and conditioning coach in 2010 before being promoted to head of strength and conditioning in 2017. He’s stayed on so long because he’s extremely popular with players and rates highly in NFLPA surveys, but I’m convinced his staff are doing something that leads to Washington’s players being more injury prone, perhaps by over-training them. An outlier injury rate over 17 years can’t be simple bad luck. I would order a full external evaluation of the team’s strength & conditioning program and make major changes there. Q: Who are you happier to see fail this season: The Cowboys or the Eagles? A: It’s a delight to see both of them fail, but more so the Eagles. The Eagles have come to be seen by people around the NFL as the “class of the division” and their fans love to loudly reiterate that belief. It’s great seeing them get taken down a peg with a nightmare season most didn’t see coming. I’ve noticed there’s a bit of an age gap in how people respond to this question. Most fans over 50ish years of age hate the Cowboys more and still vividly remember “we want Dallas” chants and the heyday of the rivalry from the 80s and 90s, but I think younger fans would generally prefer to watch the Eagles flounder. Q: What’s your happiest memory of the Washington team over the last 30 years? What’s been the pinnacle of being a fan of this team since the mid 90s? A: Honestly, my happiest memory in that time period was when Dan Snyder finally sold the team. His rotten ownership had been the millstone around the team’s neck that prevented it from ever rising up and ensured it was always surrounded by negative drama. Most fans by that point knew we’d never be a serious football operation with Dan Snyder in charge, so the sale was the first real light after a long period of darkness that signalled things could finally change. I wasn’t prepared for how quickly that would happen though, because then followed the Commanders 2024 season with a dynamic rookie QB. That season blew out anything that happened under the Dan Snyder era: first time the team won 12 regular-season games since the ’91 Super Bowl team, first time the team made the NFC Championship game since the ’91 team, etc. In addition, so many of those games ended in exciting, last-minute wins that the team got the nickname “Cardiac Commanders.” That season was the pinnacle of being a fan of the team since the mid-90s. The victory over the Lions in the playoffs was the single best game, because nobody expected us to boat race the Lions and advance to the conference championship like that.

stories.title: Saints release RB Kendre Miller
stories.summary: The Saints, on the last day before their first game since Week 7, have made a change.
stories.detailText: The Saints, on the last day before their first game since Week 7, have made a change. Via Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.football, the Saints have waived running back Kendre Miller. Miller arrived as a third-round pick (71st overall) out of TCU in 2023. He has 184 career carries for 656 yards, a per-carry average of 3.56 yards. He also has 29 career catches for 217 yards. The Saints presumably tried to trade Miller but found no takers. He'll now go to waivers. If he clears waivers, he'll become a free agent. Travis Etienne, who arrived in free agency, remains on injured reserve with a hamstring injury. The Saints currently have Alvin Kamara, C.J. Donaldson, and Audric Estimé on the depth chart. Estimé arrived recently on waivers from the Browns. The 2-5 Saints host the 5-3 Browns on Sunday. The Saints hope to avoid their first 0-4 start at home since 1980 (not including the "home" game in Paris). That year, the Saints went 0-8 at home.

stories.title: Five Washington Commanders players key to beating Rams in NFL Week 9
stories.summary: Count Stefon Diggs, Nick Cross among the Commanders who must step up and play well vs. Rams at Northwest Stadium
stories.detailText: The Commanders are looking for their first winning streak. They’ve only won two games thus far, and they weren’t earned in a row. While Washington simply must start stacking wins, they’ve been competitive while playing four quarters of football. That will be a requirement to beat an L.A. Rams team with a so-so record but tons of star power, including quarterback Matt Stafford and defensive linemen Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett. Beating L.A. on Sunday at Northwest Stadium would secure that win streak. All those dudes wear gold jackets someday. They’re also missing some key players, including Davonte Adams and Jaylen Warren on injured reserve. The Commanders IR list is also a who’s who, with Daron Payne, Laremy Tunsil, Terry McLaurin and Javon Kinlaw unavailable now and in the long-term. The Commanders will need important role players to step up and play huge in this one. Quarterback Jayden Daniels is the most obvious, so we’ll leave him off this list, but we’ll list five more players to watch in Sunday’s key NFC matchup at Northwest Stadium. WR Stefon Diggs Dan Quinn was frank about the Commanders giving Antonio Williams more opportunities with Terry McLaurin done for the season. That was no smokescreen. The third-round rookie led the team with seven targets during Week 8. He’s playing but remains someone new to the pro game. Stefon Diggs is the real No. 1 around here now. He has five touchdowns, but his 61.4% catch rate is the lowest of his career (just barely). While catch rate isn’t exclusively a receiver stat, he and Jayden Daniels must find greater sync. Look, he won’t be the dominant player of a few years back and the Commanders will spread the ball around. Diggs’ leadership has been excellent. His production needs an uptick starting on Sunday. EDGE K’Lavon Chaisson K’Lavon Chaisson has been Washington’s best edge defender this season, leading the team in overall pressures while producing against the run and pass. This is a game where quick pressures are essential and the Commanders might not blitz as much as expected considering Rams quarterback Matt Stafford’s ability to beat it. Odafe Oweh could’ve easily made this list, but the Commanders need an impact from both sides of the defensive front. DL Johnny Newton This is a bit of a speculative inclusion because Johnny Newton is reportedly getting activated , but hasn’t been formally activated off injured reserve as of this story’s publication. He has practiced for two weeks and fully heading into Week 9. Washington needs him after seeing Javon Kinlaw and Daron Payne land on season-ending injured reserve. Newton joined the Commanders with high expectations as a 2024 second-round NFL draft pick . He hasn’t lived up to them thus far, though a torn pectoral muscle from this preseason certainly set that effort back. It’s always curious how much a player returning off injured reserve can provide in terms of snap volume, but snap quality must be there. Stafford’s a true pocket passer and the fastest way to disrupt those guys is through interior pressure, forcing a quick throw, flushing him from the pocket or a sack. The Commanders defensive line was good last week against Philadelphia, especially Charles Omenihu and Shy Tuttle. Adding some juice on critical downs especially could be beneficial to a team that’ll need some game-changing plays. TE John Bates This may seem like an odd add, including someone with just five catches for 27 yards all season, but hear us out. The Rams have some heft off the edge, especially with Myles Garrett’s return off injured reserve. That man’s the best edge rusher on the planet and will require extra attention. At times, it’s a tight end one-on-one. That’s never a good matchup for anyone. Bates is one of the blocking tight ends around – he was dealing with a shoulder injury this week but didn’t receive a designation — and could be an important part of the pass protection. We could throw the Commanders running backs into this effort, especially with Aaron Donald working from the inside. Washington lost its best pass protecting back in Jeremy McNichols, but Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler must hold it down as the last line of defense. S Nick Cross Defensive coordinator Daronte Jones loves moving Nick Cross around his alignment . He’s a blitzer, an active run defender in the box, a slot cornerback and a deep safety. Cross is impactful in most every area, and has been a vital addition since returning from an illness that caused hospitalization in Week 2. The Commanders need to take the ball, set up third-and-unmanageable and then win on critical downs. Having a versatile defensive back be an unpredictable, roving chess piece should help those efforts. Who else would you in your list of Commanders to watch during Sunday’s game against L.A.? Let us know in the comments below.

stories.title: Chicago Bears Question of the Day: Which teams scare you?
stories.summary: The Bears are quickly rising up the ranks - but that doesn’t mean they are top dogs yet.
stories.detailText: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 19: George Kittle #85 of the San Francisco 49ers runs onto the field prior to the game against the Washington Commanders at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears are hitting a fever pitch at the moment. A year and a half of Ben Johnson has produced a lot of quality football, but in consecutive weeks the Bears have confidently disposed of the two teams playing in the 2025 Super Bowl. The addition of Jeffery Simmons, improvement of Caleb Williams, and a litany of talent on both sides of the ball have finally earned the Bears some serious respect across the league. As noted in Sam’s article earlier this week , the Bears are being ranked by various outlets anywhere from #7 to #2. They are being viewed as a legitimate title threat. Still, the NFL’s product is based in parity and chaos. There are still a ton of teams that can win the Super Bowl this season. However, that doesn’t mean that they are all scary to an Bears fanbase growing in confidence. Halloween has come and gone, but scary season is still upon us. Which leads me to my question. Which NFL teams still scare you? I think I can sort these teams into two different categories. Rationally scary and irrationally scary. Rationally Scary Teams This is a short list. These are the teams that I think are as good or better than the Bears right now and could beat them in a 1-on-1 matchup. San Francisco 49ers: The Niners are still the best team in football in my eyes. Shanahan remains the gold standard for head coaching, and he has morphed Brock Purdy into the perfect on-field extension of him. They are talented, fast, smart, and can beat you in a ton of ways. They are the best in the league. Buffalo Bills: The Bills are elite and will remain elite so long as they have the best QB in the league, Josh Allen, at the helm. Add in talents like Deone Walker and Gregory Rousseau making waves on defense, and the Bills are legit. Jacksonville Jaguars: I’m not overlooking you, Coach Cohen! The Jags have the 4th-best scoring offense and 2nd-best scoring defense in the league. They’re a fantastic team top to bottom that have beaten good teams like the Bengals, Patriots, and Ravens (still good even without Lamar). Irrationaly Scary Teams Detroit Lions: I think the Lions have a bottom 10 defense in the league. Outside of some talents like Aidan Hutchinson, Alim McNeil, and Brian Branch the defense is going to cost the Lions a lot of games. However, the Bears are 0-2 against the Lions since Ben Johnson has taken over, and that offense is still among the league’s best. While I think the Bears are the better team, the Lions still feel like the boogeyman. Green Bay Packers: Again, the Bears (with QB1) are the better team than the Packers. They are more complete in the trenches, and have a better QB/Coach pairing. Still, watching Jordan Love just heave bombs 40 yards downfield and assume that his WRs would beat our secondary terrifies me. A few broken coverages can change the entire shape of a season; just ask Chris Conte. Minnesota Vikings: Again…I think the Bears are far and away the more complete team. The Vikings are the inverse of the Lions. Super talented on defense and just wildly inconsistent on offense. Similarly, they have some talents on offense, namely Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, TJ Hockenson, and their two tackles, Christian Darrisaw and Brian O’Neil. But the well below average QB play from Kyler Murray has put their ceiling in doubt. As long as Brian Flores is coaching that defense, and KOC is eeking out enough offense, I will have my fears in playing the Vikings. Let’s be clear. The Bears look like they can win it all this season. Even the teams listed above are beatable if the Bears play the way we know they are capable. Stringing together wins against teams like these is another thing. Scary? Maybe a little. But we have Caleb Williams, Jeffery Simmons, and Ben Johnson, so I am sleeping well at night.

stories.title: Rams activate Myles Garrett, put Jaylen Watson on IR
stories.summary: Myles Garrett is officially back on the Rams' active roster.
stories.detailText: Myles Garrett is officially back on the Rams' active roster. The Rams announced on Saturday that they have activated Garrett from injured reserve. Head coach Sean McVay had already confirmed that the linebacker will play for the first time since Week 1 and the roster move clears the way for him to take the field against the Commanders on Sunday. Running back Ronnie Rivers will also be available after being activated from injured reserve. Tight end Terrance Ferguson was expected back as well, but was scratched on Friday with a hamstring injury. Cornerback Jaylen Watson will not play as he suffered a season-ending shoulder injury. He was placed on injured reserve Saturday and the Rams also elevated long snapper Jake McQuaide and cornerback Damarion Williams from the practice squad.

stories.title: Deshaun Watson clears concussion protocol, remains questionable for Sunday
stories.summary: Shedeur Sanders will start against the Saints.
stories.detailText: Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson won't be starting Sunday's game against the Saints, but he could be active as Shedeur Sanders's backup. The Browns announced on Saturday that Watson, who returned to practice Friday, has cleared concussion protocol. He is still listed as questionable to be available on Sunday, however. Browns head coach Todd Monken announced Sanders will start on Friday, but declined to say whether Watson will be active as the No. 2. Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green are both on the 53-man roster and could serve in that role. The Browns also announced that they have signed defensive lineman Sam Kamara to the active roster and that they have elevated tight end Carsen Ryan from the practice squad for the game in New Orleans.

teamStories.title: What is San Francisco 49ers’ offense missing without Mike Evans in Week 9 against the Las Vegas Raiders?
teamStories.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders face a tough test in Week 9, squaring off against the NFC-leading San Francisco 49ers. To preview the game, Silver and Black […
teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders face a tough test in Week 9 , squaring off against the NFC-leading San Francisco 49ers . This will be an opportunity for the Raiders to announce themselves as a legitimate playoff contender heading into the second half of the season, but that won’t come easy. To preview the game, Silver and Black Pride reached out to our friends at Niners Nation, and Kyle Posey was kind enough to answer a few questions about the 49ers for Raider Nation. Q: With the 49ers, we have to start with injuries. Granted, the team had its bye last week to heal up. So, what’s the status of San Francisco’s key players who have been banged up recently? Also, should the Raiders be worried about playing next to the ominous electrical substation? A: General manager John Lynch has already ruled out Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel for this game. It seems like their WR2, Demarcus Robinson, will return. The team will still be short-handed at wide receiver. The injury report is forever lengthy with this team. Christian McCaffrey will likely be listed as questionable, although he’s expected to play. I wouldn’t bank on seeing a heavy workload from CMC, even if it’s after a bye week. The good news is that the 49ers are getting Nick Bosa back; it appears. He’s the engine of the defense. There are a couple of role players who will have questionable designations. One is safety Marques Sigle, who started every game up until an injury in Week 4. It seems like he’s on track to return, but he may not get his spot back. Maybe the Niners put some voodoo on the substation during their bye so it can finally stop zapping this team with injuries. Q: On a related note, wide receiver Mike Evans was the 49ers’ biggest offseason addition but likely won’t play on Sunday. What is the offense missing without Evans, and who needs to step up to fill his shoes? A: Evans is everything the 49ers could have imagined, and then some. He has an explosive play rate of 29.6%. Brock Purdy probably feels like he can throw it to Evans blindfolded and still have the confidence that he’d come down with the reception. Evans has kept the offense on the field countless times on third downs. He’s averaging 17.2 yards per reception on non-red zone targets. He’s objectively been their biggest asset on offense, the same offense that’s No. 1 in most advanced statistics. There isn’t an Evans replacement on the roster, which is the problem. Not that any team would be able to replace its best player, but the Niners go from 6’5” Evans to sub-6′ Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing, or second-year pro Jordan Watkins. Robinson is “fine” as a WR2, but when he was the primary target in 2025, the offense still sputtered. The easy answer is George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey need to step up, but this could be a game where Watkins sees the most targets he has all season. Q: While everyone knows about Christian McCaffrey at this point, McCaffrey’s rushing attempts are down from 18.3 per game in 2025 to 12.0 so far in 2026 . Presumably, that’s because of rookie running back Kaelon Black’s emergence. What can you tell us about Fernando Mendoza’s college teammate’s role in the 49ers’ offense? Is Kyle Shanahan shifting toward a two-running-back approach with McCaffrey turning 30 years old this summer? (Photo by Doug Murray/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images" data-portal-copyright="Icon Sportswire via Getty Images" /> A: Black out-carried McCaffrey in Week 1, and everybody thought that’s how things would be all season. Shanahan has made it a point to reduce McCaffrey’s role after an insane workload in 2025. He’s done a good job of resisting the urge to give CMC a 25- 30-touch game. It won’t be easy to continue that without Evans, but Black could go a long way in making sure McCaffrey stays healthy. The rookie hasn’t offered much of anything in the passing game. He’s been OK as a runner. He’s a tough kid who gets yards after contact, but the big-play ability that we saw in college has been lacking. That changed last game, when Black ripped off a 30-yard run. Perhaps that’ll give him the confidence needed moving forward. I’d say Black was mildly disappointing through the first month, but improved the past two games. I’d also imagine he gets a semi-decent workload with McCaffrey nursing an injury. Q: A little more than six years after trading him to Indianapolis, DeForest Buckner came back to San Francisco via trade last week. Why was this move needed, and what do you expect to see from Buckner in his return? A: The 49ers have been decimated by injury along the defensive line. Both their starters at defensive tackle hit the injured reserve. They’ve been rotating a pass-rush first player, a rookie, and a second-year undrafted free agent at those spots for over a month. You could see last game how gassed their tackles were. Buckner is a player who rarely comes off the field. The trickle-down effect of having him in the lineup will make everybody else better because they don’t have to play in roles where they can’t shine. I think Buckner is going to look like one of the biggest deadline steals when we look back, because he’s precisely what the Niners need at defensive tackle. He’s a force as a pass rusher, and strong enough to hold his own against the run. I expect big things from Buckner. Q: Normally, putting a linebacker on Brock Bowers is a bad idea. However, Fred Warner is on a different level and might be the exception. How do you think those two match up against each other, and/or do you think 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris will go with a different strategy against Bowers? A: It’s best on best. Bowers is arguably the best skill player in the NFL. He’s amazing. Warner has held the title of best linebacker all decade. But he hasn’t really been used in man-to-man situations, and I don’t think that changes here. Klint Kubiak is smart enough to move Bowers around the formation; that way, you can’t key on him. It’ll be one of the biggest challenges the 49ers have faced in some time. The Falcons had success dinking and dunking their way downfield. I know that’s not how the Raiders use Bowers, but quick passes are the way to get over on the Niners, as they go out of their way to take away the deep pass. I’d imagine it’s a 10+ target game for Bowers. How his yardage looks is another story, but he should find success against the Niners’ zone coverage. The defense has not fared well when it comes to its nickels and safeties in coverage.

teamStories.summary: 49ers and Raiders head coaches linked since 1994 as the family times run deep between the Shanahan’s and Kubiak’s
teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Want to a crystal clear example of the kind of football team Klint Kubiak wants his Las Vegas Raiders to become? Eye the San Francisco 49ers very closely this Sunday. Because when Kubiak’s Raiders head to Santa Clara to go toe-to-to with Shanahan’s Niners, you’ll get a bird’s eye view a San Francisco team that plays complementary football and is 6-1 overall because of it. There have been fleeting moments of this for Las Vegas, however, the inability to harness consistency is a big reason why the team is 4-4 overall. Curious as to why Shanahan’s football team is one to model for Kubiak? The pair of head coaches are steeped in the game, thanks to the coaching connection between their fathers Mike Shanahan and Gary Kubiak. The Kyle and Klint dynamic goes back to 1994 when Mike was the offensive coordinator and Gary the quarterbacks coach of the 49ers Super Bowl-winning coaching staff. The elder Shanahan and Kubiak continued to be tied at the hip with the Denver Broncos. “Not a first one. Just really fortunate to grow up in that environment,” Klint Kubiak said on a first memory he had with Kyle Shanahan with their dads coaching together. “I didn’t know it at the time, but I got to be exposed to a lot of football at a young age, and I’m very grateful for that, myself and my brothers.” When Gary became the Houston Texans head coach, he gave Kyle his start as an offensive coordinator. And, in 2023, Kyle and Klint joined forces where the Kubiak was the passing game coordinator with the Shanahan dialing up the offense as head coach. Source confirms former Broncos QB coach Klint Kubiak is joining 49ers offensive staff in some capacity. Dad Gary Kubiak was a top assistant for Mike Shanahan during 49er/Bronco heydays in 90s. Now son Klint working for Kyle Shanahan (as is Kay Kubiak). #9sports — Mike Klis (@mikeklis) February 16, 2023 There’s mutual respect and trust between the two families. And with a storied history together, similarities were bound to happen. Foundationally, Shanahan’s and Kubiak’s respective offenses are deeply rooted in the same coaching tree. It’s a philosophy designed to scheme play makers open with pre-snap motions and a balanced attack that showcases a physical and productive ground game. Specializing in the outside/wide-zone run scheme, the 49ers and Raiders eat off play action and the pre-snap motions both play callers habitually use not only identify and stress coverage schemes, but get pass catchers open. Shanahan and Kubiak know to use running backs and tight ends in a variety of ways, so much so, that pass catching tailbacks and tight ends are often primary targets when the aerial attack is dialed up. As the longstanding relationship between the two is undeniable, what’s also without question is the two having their own distinct twist of the Shanahan-Kubiak offense. Klint, for example, blended modern, rhythm-based passing concepts into the time-tested zone play-action tenets the system offers. Taking into account the history between the two and the inherent competitiveness between them, beating Shanahan’s 49ers this Sunday would be quite the feather in Kubiak’s cap. Even now, there’s another branch in the Shanahan-Kubiak dynamic as Klint’s brother Klay is the 49ers offensive coordinator. 49ers offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak talks about coaching against his brother, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak, on Sunday: "He's rooting for a good competition and a good handshake after the game." 🎥: @49ers #RaiderNation | #FTTB pic.twitter.com/9N5yNGGqHt — Vegas Sports Today (@VegasSportsTD) November 6, 2026 Like Shanahan, Kubiak won’t be alone in his endeavor to coach his team past the 49ers and get his Raiders to back-to-back wins and a 5-4 record instead of a 4-5 mark. Kubiak’s chosen defensive coordinator — Rob Leonard — and special teams coordinator — Joe DeCamillis — must hold up their ends of the bargain in order to play complementary football against a really good 49ers team coming off its bye week. San Francisco is eyeing winning it’s seventh game of the year as a proper bounce back from getting beat by the Atlanta Falcons 29-20 two Sunday’s ago. Las Vegas’ defense will have its hand full stopping Shanahan and the fact Leonard’s group is a cellar dweller statistically league-wise . Playing with much more discipline and urgency, alongside Leonard dialing up blitzes, is a must as the Raiders defense has allowed 30 or more points in the last five games. “Well, I think if you’ve worked in the NFL long enough, then that’s the reality of our business. It’s a production business,” Kubiak said of the confidence he has in Leonard. “It’s the most competitive industry that I know of, and any time that you start to feel comfortable, then you will be quickly humbled. And so, whether you’re having success or you’re working to get better, if your mindset stays the same and you continue to push and push through the hard times, you come out on the other end. So, that’s the NFL. The NFL brings adversity and makes you answer to it every day.” Offensively, Kubiak has veteran Kirk Cousins at quarterback producing 19 touchdown passes (second most int he league) to just five interceptions. Brock Bowers remains a reliable target for Cousins and is a difficult cover for cornerbacks and safeties, alike. At the league meeting, 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan said #Raiders HC Klint Kubiak is an "asset" to any player he has worked with. "Anybody who has been coached by Klint truly appreciates the type of person he is." — Ryan McFadden (@ryanmcfadden_) March 30, 2026 Cousins speaks highly of the 49ers defense led by Raheem Morris, a defensive coach that left an impression on the Raiders quarterback during their time together with the Washington Commanders. “It’s a great group. They’re well coached. Fred Warner is one of the best linebackers in the league. (Nick) Bosa, Buck (DeForest Buckner), several of these guys are some of the best D-linemen in the league, and I think the secondary is also a very good group,” Cousins said about Morris’ 49ers defense. “They’ve made a lot of plays, so it’s all three levels. You see the safeties really play hard, play fast. They’ll strike you. “So, it’s a defense that played really well last year, playing really well this year. I feel like I’ve seen a lot of these same players and even somewhat the same scheme going back to when Kyle [Shanahan] first got there, and they’ve got a lot of continuity, and it shows in the tape.”

5 questions with Silver and Black Pride: Is there any hope for the Raiders’ defense against the 49ers?
teamStories.summary: We talked about Kyle Shanahan and Kirk Cousins, the Raiders' defense against the Niners' offense, Las Vegas’s running back situation, and Brock Bowers.
teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images Matt Holder from Silver and Black Pride helped us out this week with five questions about this week’s matchup between the San Francisco 49ers and the Las Vegas Raiders. We talked about Kyle Shanahan and Kirk Cousins, the Raiders’ defense against the Niners’ offense, Las Vegas’s running back situation, and Brock Bowers. 1) You can’t tell the Kirk Cousins story without Kyle Shanahan. How surprising is it to see Cousins play this well, and do you think he’ll continue that this season, even if the Raiders remain one-dimensional? Heading into the season, I thought Cousins was going to be nothing more than a placeholder for Fernando Mendoza. So, I’m very shocked by how well he’s been playing and was dead wrong in the offseason. He’s one of the biggest reasons the Raiders are in the playoff picture at the halfway point of the season. You’re 100% correct that Vegas’ offense is one-dimensional, and the lack of a running game could lead to the 38-year-old starting to show his age down the stretch. But so far, there’s been no sign of regression from Cousins. He isn’t perfect; his age/lack of mobility and arm strength show up when under pressure, but he’s coming off his best game of the year last week against the Jets. 2) Is there any hope for the Raiders defense? Everybody scores against them. The 49ers won’t have Mike Evans, but it still seems like the Niners will move the ball up and down the field. How do you see the Raiders getting stops? Kyle Shanahan’s game plan can be pretty simple this week: line up in 12 or 13 personnel (or technically 21/22 personnel with Kyle Juszczyk) and pound the rock. Shanahan doesn’t even need Evans because Las Vegas’ defense can’t stop the run out of those formations. Even the Jets had success with that, as Braelon Allen averaged 7.0 yards per carry and set a career-high rushing yardage total in the first half. New York is just poorly coached and only ran the ball four times in the second half despite playing with a lead, allowing Vegas to come back in the fourth quarter. Also, the Raiders’ defense doesn’t have a legitimate answer for George Kittle. Not that tight ends have necessarily hurt them in the passing game all year, but Kittle is the best one the Raiders’ defense has faced, and the unit doesn’t have someone who I think can match up with him. Ultimately, I think San Francisco should have no problem putting up at least 30 points on Sunday. Vegas hasn’t kept an opponent under 30 since September, and the Saints put up 27 points in three quarters in Week 3. 3) What’s going on at running back? Do you think it was a mistake to take Jeanty? Did he already lose his job? Is it more about Mike Washington being good or Jeanty being bad? ESPN’s Dan Graziano reported this week that Jeanty getting two carries while Washington had 25 in New York was meant to serve as a “wake-up call” for the 2025 No. 6 overall pick. In other words, a ‘soft benching’. Also, Jeanty stupidly made a bulletin-board-material comment about the Jets’ defense — essentially saying they don’t like to tackle — so I think Klint Kubiak’s decision was at least partly punitive. Additionally, the Raiders’ running game has been terrible this season, as it was a year ago. Kubiak has tried different offensive line combinations, so he flipped the running back rotation to see how that works. Washington definitely didn’t run away with the starting job, but the offense was much better at staying on schedule with him toting the rock. The rookie doesn’t have great vision and will miss opportunities for big plays. But at least last week, he did a better job of getting what he can compared to Jeanty. Moving forward, I expect Washington to continue having a bigger workload, but I think the touches will be closer to 50/50. Personally, I’m not ready to give up on Jeanty. However, if another team was interested in giving up, say, a second-round pick for him either by Tuesday or in the offseason, I’d probably take that deal. He isn’t the biggest problem; the offensive line is, but he isn’t helping make the situation better. 4) Klint Kubiak was on the 49ers coaching staff a few years back. How do Raiders fans feel about Kubiak, and is there a real sense that he can lead this team to the playoffs in the near future? Some in Raider Nation are frustrated with Kubiak because the team started 3-0, giving some hope for the playoffs, only to see a four-game losing streak against playoff-caliber opponents in October. But I’d say those people are in the minority. Anyone who was sensible knew that this was going to be a rebuilding year for the Raiders, and they already have more wins in 2026 than 2025. That’s progress for an organization that had the No. 1 overall pick in the draft last April, especially since the No. 1 pick has barely seen the field. Sure, the Silver and Black haven’t beaten a quality opponent and are “frauds” when it comes to being a postseason contender this season. However, the team is headed in the right direction by separating itself from the bottom of the league. Overall, I think the majority of the fanbase is happy with Kubiak and feels he’s capable of leading them to the playoffs in the future. Again, this was supposed to be year one of a two-year rebuild, and the fact the Raiders are even in the postseason discussion at this stage makes it seem like the plan is ahead of schedule. 5) Is Brock Bowers better than George Kittle? Which skill players would you take over Bowers at this point? I know a trap question when I see one, LOL! Right now, I think Kittle is the better overall tight end since he’s basically a sixth offensive lineman in the running game. But to me, Bowers is the NFL’s most unique weapon in the passing game. He can beat both defensive backs and linebackers by getting open or making ridiculous contested catches and is used more like a ‘WR1’ than a typical tight end, commanding the attention of the opposing defense’s best coverage defender every week. Bowers creates a lot of matchup problems, similar to how Sean Payton used to use Jimmy Graham in New Orleans. To be honest, there aren’t many other skill players around the league that I’d take over the third-year offensive weapon. It’d have to be one of the top-tier wide receivers, like a Ja’Marr Chase or Justin Jefferson type. Bowers is just such a unicorn that it’d take a lot for me to want to give him up.
